title: 24K Whips
content: 24K Whips is a Las Vegas, Nevada boutique yo-yo string brand founded by Daniel Kessler. Specializing in custom hand-spun strings made to order, the brand built a following through its signature "faded" strings — two-toned polyester blends where two colors fade seamlessly across the strand’s length. Custom orders are available in any material, length, thickness, and color combination.Kessler’s philosophy centers on the string as the primary interface between player and yo-yo, and 24K Whips positioned itself alongside contemporaries like Zipline Strings and A&A Yoyo Strings in the boutique micro-production string market. The brand distributed primarily through direct sales via BigCartel and built its community through Instagram and Facebook.In 2018, Kessler collaborated with Rain City Skills to co-design the Retro Rocket, contributing concept direction and custom colorway-matched strings to the package. The Retro Rocket was released in early 2019 and is the only yo-yo hardware associated with the 24K Whips name.

title: 2SickYoyos
content:
2SickYoYos is an American yo-yo company founded in October 2013 by Joey Serrano, based in Easton, Pennsylvania. Joey began yo-yoing in 2008 and in Spring 2013 prototyped his first yo-yo — the Gambit — with community support from YoYoExpert Forums. The positive response led him to launch 2SickYoYos as a brand. All yo-yos are USA-made and themed around chess: every model is named after a chess piece or chess term.

2SickYoYos is known for beautiful, unique colorways and the philosophy that their yo-yos function as both toys and playable art. Notable releases include the Gambit, Queen, Bishop, Knight, King, and Guardian.

title: 3YO3
content: 3YO3 is an artisan yo-yo brand founded in 2009 by Landon Balk of Clearwater, Florida — a mechanical engineering graduate who had been hand-machining yo-yos on a manual lathe since 2004. Named after the Roland TB-303 Bass Line synthesizer, the brand became known for using unconventional materials including acrylic, Delrin, Teflon, aluminum, and titanium, most machined by hand. The brand won back-to-back WYYC Mod Contest titles (3rd in 2010 with the Hourglass, 1st in 2011 with the Grind King) and built a dedicated collector following. All 19 known models are discontinued; the last confirmed release was the Bassline 2 in June 2014.

title: 44CLASH
content: 44CLASH is an annual yo-yo freestyle competition founded in 2008 in Yokohama, Japan by Masanobu Iwata — widely regarded as the world's first yo-yo contest held in a nightclub setting. The name is a Japanese wordplay: the number 4 can be read as "yo" (ヨ), making "44" sound like "yoyo." Each event features exclusive limited-edition collaborative yo-yos produced with partner manufacturers including YoYoRecreation, YoYoFactory, Mowl, C3 Yoyo Design, Throwing Point, and others. Freestyles are scored on technique, performance, and a unique "44CLASH Point" rewarding coolness and crowd impact.

title: 44EMPORIUM
content:
44EMPORIUM is a Canadian yo-yo store and brand. The number "44" references the Japanese reading of the digits four-four ("shi-shi" → "yo-yo"). The brand produces a series of original yo-yos, including signature models for top Canadian players.

Notable releases include the Monolith — a signature for Junhong McIntosh-Lee, a tri-material throw (6061 aluminum + stainless steel + POM) weighing 73.4g — and the Feather, a lightweight competition bi-metal (7075 Al + SS, 55.5g) signature for Evan Cui, who placed 2nd at the 2024 Canadian Nationals with it.

title: A-RT (Alternate Return Tops)*
content:
Alternate Return Tops (A-RT) is a Canadian yo-yo design venture founded in 2016 by Jensen Kimmitt and Charles Haycock, both formerly of the CLYW competitive team. The brand launched with a late-2015 fundraising bundle (Junior, Peon, Orphan) and has since operated as a small, irregular-drop label rather than a continuous retail catalog, distributing historically through Shopify with resale support from Yoyo Store Rewind (Japan) and, more recently, direct through its own WooCommerce storefront at a-rt.ca. Known for irreverent branding and limited small-batch releases, including collaborations with SF Yoyos, At Design Lab, and Toki-Yo.

* Editorial Note on Brand Controversy: Readers should be aware that A-RT (A Return To Things) and its founders have faced significant criticism and community division regarding business practices and interpersonal conduct. Specifically, the brand drew heavy backlash for its origins and branding overlap with pre-existing independent entities, alongside controversies surrounding dismissive responses to community intellectual property concerns. While A-RT remains culturally influential and retains a dedicated following for its unique approach to throw design, these ethical and professional friction points have led various community members and independent enthusiasts to distance themselves from the brand.

title: Abbe Toys
content: Abbe Toys was an Australian maker of the Black Mamba yo-yos, which were imported to the US during the late-1990s boom. The Yo-Yo Museum documents the Black Mamba, whose auto-return Yo-Matic mechanism was licensed to Tomy for the Japanese Screw Ball. The company later rebranded to PhatYo. Its founding year, city and current status are unknown.

title: AceYo
content: AceYo is a Chinese yo-yo studio founded in 2013, producing high-performing yo-yos at accessible price points. The brand is best known for its Gravitation line of budget mono-metals and the Mercy line of competition-ready bi-metals, alongside premium titanium, tri-metal, and hybrid plastic models. AceYo sponsors Asian competitions and has built an international following through signature models for Veronika Kamenská, Hong Teng Long, and Zhang Suze.

title: Alchemik
content:
Step into the realm of Alchemik Yoyos, where the art of yoyoing transcends performance to become a transformational experience. 

Founded in 2023 by Jaxon Watts, the goal of Alchemik yoyos is to unite the different spheres of the yoyo community in the pursuit of something new. Our team consists of players, club leaders, and just generally good folks from several continents with the goal of providing a unique, holistic perspective on yoyo design and play. Those who wear the Alchemik jersey each play their own role in crafting our throws, a reflection of our individual personalities. Starting with the now iconic Tyrant, our goal is to push the limits of performance while crafting yoyos for everyday use, where each throw reminds you of your innate creative power and the ability to create something new.

Alchemik yoyos - Transform your play

title: Alox Manufacturing Company
content: Alox Manufacturing Company of St. Louis, Missouri began in 1919 as a shoelace maker, according to the YoYo Wiki, which cites Lucky Meisenheimer's collectors guide, and expanded into kites, marbles and jump ropes. A 1938 St. Louis magazine account supports the company and its founder. The wiki says it entered yo-yos during the 1930s craze without lathes of its own, buying yo-yo halves from other makers and painting and assembling them. Its Flying Disk and Jeweled Flying Disk are listed.

title: “alternatives”
content: "alternatives" is a Southeast Asian competition yo-yo brand founded in 2023 by Swee Jim Ho, a Malaysian competitor who returned to the hobby after a seven-year break. Built around a roster of Southeast Asian and international champions, the brand emphasises power, stability, and unconventional material combinations. The name references finding different possibilities. Products are competition-grade with novel constructions including bi-metal, tri-metal, and aluminium-plus-polycarbonate hybrids.

title: American Spinners
content: American Spinners was founded in 1988 by Bill Cress, according to the Smithsonian, and a contemporary article places it in Wayne, New Jersey. It made one-piece wooden yo-yos with exotic finishes, including the Standard and the Pocket Rocket, which the Yo-Yo Museum lists. The YoYo Wiki, citing Lucky Meisenheimer's guide, says production continued as late as 1999. Its current status is unverified.

title: Anomaly Yo-Yos
content:
Anomaly Yo-Yos is a small-batch American independent yoyo brand operating under the motto "Decisively unique." Founded around 2018–2019, the brand distinguished itself through unconventional shapes and premium materials — notably a full stainless steel monometal (the Euphonious) at a time when aluminum dominated boutique releases. Sales ran primarily through Instagram and at competitions rather than conventional retail, lending the brand a collector-circuit reputation.

Anomaly produced three solo models — the titanium H-shape Onomatopoeia, the stainless steel organic Euphonious, and the undersized D-bearing Fallen Angel — before collaborating with GWAY Throws (Guy With A YoYo) on two releases: the Saboteur and the Daredevil, both in 2021. The brand went on hiatus later that year, citing hopes to return; as of 2026 no new releases have been confirmed.

title: Anti-Yo
content:
Founded by Kiya Babzani and Sonny Patrick, Anti-Yo is based in San Francisco, California. Many thought the company was dead for a while before they came back with a 2011 release. Since then not much has happened, and while there is no confirmation, it seems 2015 is when the company stopped doing anything.

More information coming soon.

Wesley Cheng Mods

Wesley Cheng does great yoyo mods.  Find him on Instagram @yoyospirit, or on Facebook.  The following yoyos were powder coated and/or modded by him.

title: AnY
content: AnY is described by the YoYo Wiki as a maker formed in 2005 by a group of Korean and Taiwanese yo-yoers, producing small runs of high-end metal yo-yos in South Korea. Its early models, the QuickSilver and MiRoC, used an "O-Pad" variant of YoYoJam's patented o-ring response. The MiRoC was sold in the US in very limited numbers through YoYoNation. The founding date and its current status are not independently confirmed.

title: Aoda Toys
content: The YoYo Wiki describes Aoda Toys as a Chinese toy maker whose yo-yos were reported as copies of Auldey designs, which in turn copied Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo. It lists models such as the Shadow Arc and Flying Eagle. These details come from the wiki alone and are not independently confirmed.

title: Arc1
content: Arc1 is a Netherlands-based creative studio — video production, photography, and industrial design — founded in Zutphen in 2011 by Dan (forum handle: Grapes). The company launched its first yoyo in September 2022, presenting its throws as functional art designed aesthetics-first. The Gemstones was the first modern Dutch-made unresponsive yoyo, developed in collaboration with Mark Diehr of MK1 YoYos on CAD design and the interchangeable spin-top cap system.

title: Ardeus
content:
Ardeus is a maker of handcrafted 3D-printed fixed-axle yo-yos, operated by a maker based in the Philippines who is active on the YoYoExpert Forums as "Ardeus." Each yo-yo is 3D-printed and assembled with a hickory axle (1/4" or 5/16"), and features Ardeus's signature "tic-tac" 8-hole response system. Orders are placed directly through YoYoExpert forum threads.

The lineup consists of a related family of models: the Stroll, Stroller, Sprint, Stride, Strider, Stomp, Stompling, and Skip — each varying in size, weight, and profile while sharing the same handcrafted construction. Ardeus ships internationally, though shipping to the US was suspended August 2025–February 2026 due to a postal service disruption.

title: Aroundsquare
content: Aroundsquare Ltd. was incorporated in 2008 in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. The company is primarily known as a maker of minimalist skill toys and EDC (everyday-carry) gear, and is a foundational figure in modern begleri — they co-produced the widely-viewed 2016 film "2 Beads 1 String" and founded the Single Grip Open (2016) and Sling Slam (2019) begleri freestyle contests. Founder credit goes to Matthew Hiebert per independent trade-press interviews (not stated on the brand's own About page). In August 2026 Aroundsquare released its first-ever yo-yo, "Not Machine," a nostalgic fixed-axle wooden throw pitched as a casual EDC item rather than a competitive performance yoyo.

title: Astral Return Tops
content: Astral Return Tops is an independent yo-yo brand that released its debut throw, The Particle, in 2022. The Particle is a full-size 6061 aluminum mono-metal designed as a capable, well-rounded performer — featuring a profile between H and V shape, a blast finish for grinds, and cup geometry engineered for fingerspins and inner ring grinds. Yo-yos sold through Astral's own Square storefront and select retailers, packaged in a premium wooden box with carrying pouch.

title: At Design Lab
content: At Design Lab is an independent yo-yo design studio founded in 2021 and based in Tokyo, created by a designer who goes by "At." The brand operates as a self-described "CtoC experimental brand" — a quiet creative space rather than a conventional business — with a philosophy rooted in Tokyo's fast-shifting cultural scene: "new things are born, only to shift and fade in the blink of an eye."The name "At" represents three ideas: the Origin of creation, the Intersection where ideas meet, and the Singularity from which unexpected value emerges. The brand's guiding design philosophy is borrowed from Leonardo da Vinci — "Simplicity is the Ultimate sophistication" — expressed in their "From collection to selection" approach: proposing that players choose one or two yo-yos they genuinely love rather than accumulating many.At Design Lab draws deep inspiration from classic yo-yo designs of the past — particularly the CLYW Peak, YoYoJam Hitman, Anti-yo (Eetsit, Bapezilla, YWET, Business, Sparrow), Duncan Butterfly, Duncan Freehand, and HSpin Pyro — and treats these archetypes as starting points for contemporary refinement rather than competition-spec optimization. Products are typically released in extremely limited runs (often 100 units worldwide), sell out within minutes, and are offered in a small number of carefully considered colorways. The brand also produces proprietary coatings — Smooth Ultimatte, Vintage, Snow, Silky, and Aging (nickel/copper) — applied as deliberate surface treatments that affect playing feel as well as aesthetics.Collaborations have become a significant part of the brand's identity: partnerships include A-RT (Alternate Return Tops, Canada) on the BRICC (2025) and HSpin (Switzerland) on the Pyro OG (2026), a faithful re-issue of the original 2005 HSpin Pyro marking its 20th anniversary.

title: Atmos Projects
content:
Atmos Projects is a minimalist yo-yo design brand founded in July 2020. The brand specializes in high-performance yo-yos focused on organic shapes, unique playfeel, and aesthetics. The founder came into yo-yoing around 2006, initially playing 5A before transitioning to 1A. Atmos is based in the Asia-Pacific region and is known for thoughtful design journals published alongside each release.

Notable releases include the Noah, Abel, Cephas, Snowberry (their first plastic), Lamina, Fuji, Cloudberry, and the Noma — a collaboration with legendary Japanese player Tsukasa Takatsu (One Drop team, "things that repeat" trick movement). Atmos also produces the SPHERE, a community project and resource platform.

title: Aufheben
content: Aufheben is a Japanese yo-yo brand that began on 6 June 2019, according to Yo-Yo Store REWIND, with its own site listing a base in Fujisawa, Kanagawa. Owner Kazuki Morii designs the yo-yos, and its first model was the Eureka, followed by the Shelter. Its higher-grade "Sync by Aufheben" line includes the Nurture, Morii's signature model. It has released models through 2026.

title: Augment Design
content: Augment Design (Augment Yoyos) is a niche sub-label launched by Thesis Yoyos in February 2022 for smaller, experimental, direct-sale-only projects. Its first and, to date, only release was the CALYX, a Grade 5 titanium competition throw sold directly through Thesis's own site in a limited run. The brand's Instagram has been dormant since mid-2022 with no further releases surfacing since.

title: Auldey Toys
content:
About Auldey

Auldey Toys was founded in December 1993 by Cai Dongqing in Chenghai, Shantou, Guangdong, China — the region known as "China Toy and Gift City." The company initially rose to dominance by producing and selling unlicensed copies of Tamiya Mini 4WD cars, establishing a massive distribution network across China and Southeast Asia. In 1999, capitalizing on the Hyper Yo-Yo craze sweeping East Asia, Auldey launched its "Super Yo-Yo" (超级悠悠) line — predominantly clones of Yomega and Bandai/Duncan models — bringing competition-style yo-yos to the Chinese mass market at accessible price points.

In 2004 Auldey founded Alpha Animation Co., Ltd. to produce animated content promoting its toys. In 2006 the company launched the live-action TV franchise Blazing Teens (火力少年王), tying a generation of branded yo-yo products directly to an aspirational TV narrative. This strategy proved transformative: Blazing Teens aired across China and expanded to South Korea, the Philippines, Malaysia, and other Southeast Asian markets by 2007, making "Audi" (Auldey's Japanese market name) a household name for competitive yo-yoing throughout Asia. The company simultaneously upgraded from clone production to original engineering, sponsoring Chinese champion Yicheng Luo starting in 2008 — who used the Auldey L3 to place 4th at the 2008 World Yo-Yo Contest, the best finish ever at that time for a Chinese player.

Through the 2010s Auldey developed a series of high-performance metal throws endorsed by international champions, most notably 2011 World Champion Marcus Koh (Singapore), whose Ares Star, Magnum, and Equilibrium signature models were sold globally through specialist retailers. The company also produced notable collaborations with YOYOFFICER (Orbis, 2015) and Turning Point of Japan (Positron, 2014). Auldey hosted the 2018 World Yo-Yo Contest in Shanghai and produced commemorative souvenir yo-yos. Into the 2020s the brand continues releasing modern competition models and licensed collaborations, including a 2024 partnership with miHoYo for Honkai Impact 3rd merchandise. With the 2007 corporate restructuring into Alpha Group, Auldey's yo-yo division operates alongside animation, RC vehicles, and licensed character products under the umbrella of China's largest integrated toy-entertainment conglomerate.

title: Axis YoYos
content: Axis YoYos was a US-based yo-yo brand founded in 2015 by James Reed and Tyler Hsieh, launching with the crowdfunded Pulsefire bimetal. The brand quickly gained attention for a novel quasi-multi-step stainless rim profile that optimized weight distribution in unconventional ways, and signed Yuki Nishisako — introduced via Yoshihiro Matsubara of Japan Looping Solutions — as their first sponsored player. After releasing four additional models (Pulsefire Ti, Mixtape, EX, and SAL-Ti), the brand went inactive around 2016–2017 following Tyler Hsieh's departure to co-found UNPRLD.

title: B.W.W.
content: B.W.W. is a Japanese brand owned by Tsubasa Onishi, a 4A world champion, that makes wide Delrin offstring yo-yos. Retailer records show the Wwing in 2012 and the Bulk in 2014, followed by a third model named B.W.W. around 2022. Yo-Yo Store REWIND lists the Bulk as Onishi's signature yo-yo. The brand's founding year is unconfirmed, as a first release does not establish when it started.

title: Bandai
content: Bandai is a toy manufacturer based out of Japan; known in the yo-yo community for their Hyper Yo-Yo products starting in 1997.

title: Bandalore
content:
BANDALORE is a boutique yo-yo brand whose name honors the historical term for the yo-yo. Before "yo-yo" was popularized by Pedro Flores in 1928, the term "bandalore" was used in Europe between the 17th and 19th centuries to describe a simple spinning toy of two discs connected by an axle with a string. BANDALORE's debut model, the Bandalo:re, uses the ":re" suffix to signify remake, redo, and refresh — a nod to the rebirth of that historical toy in a modern design context.

title: BC Yoyo
content:
BC Yoyo is a line of premium hardwood fixed-axle yo-yos manufactured by What's Next Mfg., Inc., founded in 1995 by Brad Countryman in Arcade, New York. The BC name derives from Brad Countryman's initials.
The company traces its roots to 1980, when Countryman began crafting yo-yos from surplus furniture wood at his Country Wood Shop. After drawing major retailer interest at the 1981 New York Toy Fair, the business grew through Hummingbird Toy Co. in the late 1980s before relaunching as What's Next in 1995 exclusively for yo-yo production. At its peak, the company manufactured 12,000 yo-yos per day and was recognized as the world's largest producer of fixed-axle wooden yo-yos and aluminum ball-bearing yo-yos. What's Next also produced the Tom Kuhn line of aluminum ball-bearing yo-yos. All BC yo-yos are made in the USA from hard maple.

title: Beer Factory
content: Beer Factory is described by the YoYo Wiki as a Chinese maker established in 2007 by Roland Yu, known as "Beer", and tied to the Beer Toy online shop. Its first yo-yo, the Love Dog, was based on the Duncan Freehand Zero with a different response system. The wiki also lists the E-Star and Spider. These details come from the wiki alone.

title: Big Brother Yo-Yos
content: Big Brother Yo-Yos was created by Douglas Spence in Woodbury, Minnesota. The Yo-Yo Museum dates its start to 2008, while the YoYo Wiki says January 2009. Documented models include the Bully, Wedgie, TT and Swirly. The company was short-lived, and no official site is known.

title: Big Red Strings
content: Big Red Strings is a family-run, handmade yo-yo string manufacturer based in Chico, California, founded in 2025 by a thrower with the surname Herringer. What started as a personal hobby making string for a slower, flowing play style became a small business offering a growing lineup of nylon, polyester, and blend strings made by throwers, for throwers.

title: BigBoi Yoyo’s
content: BigBoi Yoyo's is a small independent yo-yo accessories brand based in Florida, run by Nicholas Privett. The brand sells strings and counterweights directly through its Square storefront. In August 2026, BigBoi announced a collaboration with longtime manufacturer Spintastics Yoyos on its first full yo-yo release, the V-tour, an aggressive V-shaped competition throw roughly 18 months in development and still in production as of this writing.

title: Bird In Hand
content: Bird In Hand is a yo-yo store in downtown Chico, California, founded in 1981 and owned by Bob Malowney, who also organizes the American Nationals. Its own wooden yo-yos, turned by Steve Smith, were produced around 1988-95 and included the Award, Chico Traveller and Super Chico Tournament 77. Later US National yo-yos were made by Hummingbird and What's Next. The store is still active.

title: Boise Woodworks
content: Boise Woodworks is a Boise, Idaho workshop producing handmade wood yo-yos alongside games, ring boxes, and other small wood goods. Its yo-yos use U.S.-sourced hardwoods, sustainable exotic hardwoods, and locally sourced recycled or repurposed wood. Models include fixed-axle designs as well as ball-bearing designs with stainless-steel axles.

title: Broke Village
content: Broke Village is a small yo-yo brand founded by Cory Gardner out of Austin, Texas. Gardner is an avid fixed-axle player who identified a gap in the market for premium machined-aluminum fixed-axle yo-yos and launched the brand in 2015 with the Fidalgo. In 2019 the brand collaborated with Rain City Skills (Canada) on the Convoy, a 7075-aluminum unresponsive throw inspired by WWII-era Merchant Marine service heritage. The brand relaunched in 2024–2025 with a third yo-yo (DSCB) in production.

title: Budweiser Urban Projects
content: BU2R (Budweiser Urban Projects) is a cultural patronage platform of Budějovický Budvar, the Czech state-owned Budweiser Budvar brewery, established in 2007 to support original Czech urban culture. Projects have spanned hip-hop, documentary film, skateboarding history, and music. In 2014, BU2R partnered with Turning Point and Preciosa to produce a limited-edition crystal-studded yo-yo released exclusively at the World Yo-Yo Contest in Prague — one of 100 units made, each set with 126 hand-placed Preciosa crystals.

title: Buzz-On Industries
content:
Buzz-On Industries was started in 2003 by Dave Bazan and Dave Muehlhaeusler.

An early Buzz-On sheet.

title: C3Yoyodesign
content: C3yoyodesign is Hong Kong's first manufacturer of high-end yo-yos, founded in 2009 by Walter Wong, Ron Chan, and Simpson Wong — three experienced competitive players who had already been traveling the world photographing, filming, and promoting the yo-yo scene. Prior to building products, the team helped organize local Hong Kong events and contests. In 2011 the company formally established itself as a full manufacturer, expanding its team roster beyond Asia to include players from Europe and North America.The brand gained international recognition rapidly, driven by landmark releases: the Berserker bi-metal (2012) set a new standard for professional bi-metal design; the Krown (2013), Shinya Kido's signature, launched C3 onto the world stage and became one of the best-selling competition yo-yos in history; and the Speedaholic (2013) proved that a sub-$15 plastic could compete with metal. Since then, C3 has sponsored world champions across multiple divisions — including Shinya Kido (1A, 2009 World Champion), Shion Araya (1A, 2016–2017 World Champion), Rei Iwakura (4A, 7x World Champion), Hobbit Wen (Women's 1A, 2015 & 2018), and Sora Ishikawa (5A).C3yoyodesign operates its own in-house anodizing and handles design, engineering, and photography internally. Their product philosophy spans the full price spectrum — from the $9 Arise beginner model to the $600 Berserker Titanium world-limited edition — while maintaining a consistent reputation for exceptional build quality, colorway artistry, and competition performance. The company celebrated its 15th anniversary in 2024 with the release of the tri-material Super Scintillator, cementing its status as one of the most influential yo-yo brands in the world.

title: Canopy Collection
content:
Canopy Collection is an ambidextrous brand with a foothold in the yo-yo community.

Guided by a balance of spontaneity and intentionality, Canopy explores how yo-yo connects us all and seamlessly weaves into everyday life.

Driven to create timeless products, inspiring media, and incredible experiences, Canopy aims to celebrate the many faces that make yo-yoing unique.

meta.yya_company_profile:
How did the idea for Canopy Collection come about?

It was a crazy idea born over a post-concert Thai meal and inspired by a stainless steel tumbler.

I wrote more about our beginnings here:

https://canopy-collection.com/editorial/how-canopy-came-to-be

What does a day in the life look like for you running Canopy Collection?

Every day varies quite a bit—the busyness comes and goes. No two days are the same. One day, we might be deep in CAD, fine-tuning a design, and the next, we’re figuring out logistics for an event.

For context, a small team of us are building the brand behind the scenes. We’re all working on it part-time, balancing other commitments or jobs on the side—so it’s definitely been a juggling act.

Walk me through your creative process.

It depends—ideas come from different sources, both internally and externally. For our first year, we used the technical outdoors as a guiding theme. Outdoor brands often release product variations optimized for different use cases. Similarly, in yo-yo design, while top players can perform their full trick sets on most modern yoyos, the differences lie in the details—shape, weight distribution, and how each design caters to different playstyles.

We set out to create a universal shape that balanced competition and casual play, drawing inspiration from The Otter and the Atmos Polaris, but use material as our primarly lever. The question became: how could we use materials to enhance performance for different use cases while maintaining a consistent shape and design?

What’s your favorite memory running Canopy?

Definitely Stargazing Night! Specifically, seeing Polo beat Zach in the preliminary round of the battle. It surpassed any and all expectations we had as a team.

With the event, we wanted to create something that focused on the community—its creativity and diversity—and celebrate the people who make it so special. We aimed to build a space where everyone felt welcomed and included, while also placing creativity, originality, and musicality at the forefront.

Really grateful for how the event was received!

https://canopy-collection.com/editorial/post-stargazing-night

What’s your favorite release to date?

Personally, the Canopy SS. But I’m biased—this one most closely resembles The Otter. It has a quickness and agility that are surprising for its undersized specs.

https://canopy-collection.com/editorial/canopy-ss-design-notes

What’s your next release, and what makes it so exciting? What’s in store for Canopy Collection in the future?

We have a handful of things planned, but we’re keeping them quiet for now.

If you could go back and do one thing differently, what would it be?

Looking back, not much we’d do differently. We’ve made a ton of mistakes over the last year, but we wouldn’t be where we are today without them—and the lessons they brought! So grateful. :)

Any advice to aspiring companies/creators?

Just get something out into the community’s hands and learn from their feedback! Even if it’s just a concept or a rough sketch on a napkin. There were so many times we hesitated to release something, but the community is incredibly supportive.

And find a good team to work with!

title: Caribou Lodge Yo-Yo Works
content:
From CLYW:

"CLYW is a premium return top company based in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. Started by retired mechanical engineer Chris Mikulin in 2006, CLYW combines art, craft, and technology to create some of the best performing return tops in the world. 

CLYW is led by founder Chris Mikulin and National YoYo Master Steve Brown. Chris continues to design CLYW’s unmistakably unique return tops, while Steve manages their team and day-to-day operations.Together they work daily on creating playable art for discerning return top players, and contributing to the future of the return top industry worldwide. "

title: Channel Craft
content: Channel Craft is a Pennsylvania maker of American-made toys, games and puzzles, founded in 1983 and historically based in Ellsworth, Pennsylvania; its current contact address is in North Charleroi. Its yo-yo is a vintage-style maple model, customizable with logos and sold with "The Art of Yo" booklet, according to the Yo-Yo Museum and the YoYo Wiki.

title: Cheerio Yo-Yo & Bo-Lo Company
content: Cheerio Yo-Yo & Bo-Lo Company Ltd. was a Canadian yo-yo manufacturer based in Kitchener, Ontario. Founded in 1931 by Wilfred Schlee, Sr., the company produced wooden yo-yos and bo-los through the 1950s. In 1954, Duncan Toys acquired Cheerio, continuing the line under the Duncan brand until approximately 1963. Known for quality wooden construction and decorative variants (jeweled, gold-leaf, medallion models). A significant part of Canadian yo-yo history and North American toy manufacturing heritage.

title: Chemtoy
content: Chemtoy Corporation was based in Cicero, Illinois, according to a Canadian trademark record. The YoYo Wiki, citing Lucky Meisenheimer's collectors guide, says it made three plastic yo-yos in the late 1970s, the Crown Royal, Mark V and Number 1, sold in blister packs with a 1972 copyright date. The trademark record does not verify those models or the dates.

title: Chico Yo-Yo Company
content: Chico Yo-Yo Company (CYYC) was founded in April 2009 by Thad Winzenz, Richy Nye, and Bob Malowney in Chico, California — the historic home of the US National Yo-Yo Contest and the National Yo-Yo Museum. The company produced all of its throws locally using Pro2Pro Machining Services in Chico, releasing a series of precision-machined aluminum yo-yos built for competition and serious play. CYYC's sponsored team included Mike Marshall, Sam Ungerer, Zac Rubino, and Nate Dailey, each of whom received signature models. The brand went dormant around 2017 after approximately two dozen releases; their products are now treated as a museum collection by the yo-yo community.

title: Circle City YoYos
content: Circle City YoYos is an indie yo-yo brand founded in Indianapolis, Indiana in 2018 by a hobbyist known as Bradd. The name references Indianapolis's historic nickname "Circle City." The brand released five models — a mix of house designs and player-signature throws — built around a philosophy of blending old-school yo-yo aesthetics with modern competitive geometry. Team riders included Kyle Pearson and Cody Diehl, and the brand partnered with string makers Lifeline Strings and Bad Wolfe Co. The official website went offline sometime after the brand's fifth release, the Odium (~2022).

title: The Coca-Cola Company
content:
The Coca-Cola Company is one of the world's most recognized beverage corporations, founded in 1886 by pharmacist Dr. John Pemberton in Atlanta, Georgia. While not a yo-yo manufacturer, Coca-Cola has a rich history of yoyo promotional campaigns spanning from 1947 to the present day, making it one of the most prolific sources of collectible promotional yoyos in history.
Beginning with Jack Russell's work as a Duncan Toys demonstrator in 1947, Coca-Cola's yoyo promotions became a global phenomenon. In 1958, Jack Russell purchased the promotional yoyo business and molds from Duncan and formed his own company, which eventually became Russell Promotions Inc. — the exclusive yoyo promotional partner for Coca-Cola worldwide. Over the following decades, Russell Promotions deployed professional demonstrators across 95 countries and sold over half a billion Coca-Cola-branded yoyos globally.
The Coca-Cola yoyo campaigns sparked some of the earliest modern yoyo booms in countries including Australia, Japan, the Philippines, and Mexico. The campaigns ran through the 1990s and were revived in the 2000s and 2010s through licensed partnerships with Japanese manufacturers Matsui Gaming Machine and Freshthings.

title: Crucial
content:
From the YoYo Wiki:

"Born Crucial (or just Crucial) is owned by Paul Yath and the manufacturer one of the first Delrin yo-yos, the Milk. The company's second release the Milk 2% was released in May 2008 with a run of over 250 yo-yos. It is the same shape as the Milk, but it has more rim weight due to the fact of it's smaller SPR system and A-bearing, this in turn makes for a more stable version of the Milk. The name of the company used to be Born Crucial but now it is simply Crucial."

title: Custom Products
content: Custom Products (originally Mesa Custom Machining Corporation, also known as Custom Yo-Yo) is a precision machining company based in Gilbert, Arizona that produced a line of all-aluminum yo-yos starting in 1998. Founded in 1987 as a machine shop, the company entered the yo-yo market at the height of the late-1990s yo-yo boom, offering CNC-machined aluminum yo-yos with ball bearing axles and their proprietary Performance Ring response system. At its peak the company produced up to 75,000 yo-yos per year.Custom Products became known for two distinct product families: the butterfly-shaped AXL/AXL Elite line for string tricks, and the MAG series — a collectible run of three series featuring intricately machined side cutouts resembling automobile wheels. They also produced the compact Reactor/Chain Reactor mini yo-yos and the AXLerator, an Imperial-shaped looping yo-yo. Premium gold-plated variants — the GoldenEye (Modified shape) and GoldenFly (Butterfly shape) — were released alongside the standard models. The Chain Reactor design was developed with input from player Eric Wolff, who pioneered the response pad concept later adopted across the company's full lineup.Custom Products was sued by Playmaxx/ProYo for patent infringement related to their ball bearing and response system, a dispute that shaped the industry. By the mid-2000s the company had shifted its primary focus to paintball equipment and accessories, and yo-yo manufacturing ceased. The yo-yo product line continued to be sold through the customproducts.us website on a limited basis for years afterward, though no new models were introduced.

title: dale tubat
content:
From Dale:

"I'm a yoyo player that started in late 2010, currently sponsored by unparalleled. i began experimenting with 3d printed yoyos in 2022. there isn't really any rhyme or reason for the concepts i explore with my yoyo designs. every now and then i become inspired by stuff that happens in my life and come up with an idea that i try to execute on."

title: Damian Puckett
content: Damian Puckett is an independent American yo-yo designer who began commissioning custom designs through FPM (Yoyofriends’ parent manufacturer) around 2018. Known for performance-focused bimetals and titaniums, his releases favor heavier, larger throws with a preference for the W/wing shape. All designs are produced in limited runs and sold through third-party retailers; Puckett has no personal storefront.

title: Dedhed Designs
content: Dedhed Designs is a US-based boutique 5A counterweight brand founded in 2019 by Michael Letsom and his wife. Their signature line of horror- and creature-themed resin counterweights, branded as Dedweights, are hand-painted with alcohol inks and aerosol model paints, then finished with Cerakote aviation-grade ceramic coating for scratch and chemical resistance. The brand's mission: creating functional art — pieces you want to display just as much as you want to play. Dedhed also produces HedStandz, character resin display stands designed to hold and swap Dedweights.

title: Dell Plastics Co
content: Dell Plastics Co. was a Brooklyn, New York company that, according to the YoYo Wiki, made plastic toy soldiers and flowers before entering yo-yos in the 1960s. Its "Big D" yo-yos were sold on a "Buy a Big D" television slogan, and the Yo-Yo Museum documents them and places the end of its yo-yo line around 1965. The wiki says Duncan sued Dell and Royal, and that Dell dropped its yo-yo line rather than fight the case. Models listed include the Big D Astronaut, Flying Star, Returner, Sleeper King, Super Star and Tournament.

title: D&H Enterprises
content: D&H Enterprises was a small-batch, direct-to-consumer manufacturer of precision-machined aircraft aluminum yo-yos based in North Bend, Washington. Founded in 1999 by David and Heidi (D&H), the company produced two released models — the Raptor and the Cutlass — each in a strictly limited run of 250 serialized, engraved units. Both were CNC-machined from T-6061 aircraft aluminum with a hard-anodized two-tone finish and a shim-adjustable gap system. Three additional prototype designs (Hurricane, Sextant, Mag) were announced for a June 2000 release but never reached production. The company website went dark by early 2002.

title: Dif-e-Yo
content:
Dif-e-Yo was founded in 2001 by Frank P. Difeo (March 7, 1952 – March 3, 2024) of Bradford, Massachusetts. A precision machinist by trade, Frank trained at Haverhill Trade School and spent eighteen years as a tool maker at Lucent Technologies before retiring early to pursue yo-yo manufacturing full-time through his home shop, Difeo Machine.
Frank's defining contribution to the hobby was the patented KonKave (KK) bearing — a concave-profiled ball bearing that automatically centers the string in the gap, reducing friction and enabling longer, more stable spin. Introduced in prototype form with the Daizzy-Yo (2002), refined, patented, and licensed widely, the KonKave bearing became one of the most influential yo-yo components in history and continues to be sold by multiple distributors today.
Unlike most manufacturers, Frank used a milling machine rather than a lathe — allowing him to cut complex internal hub geometries, multi-stepped profiles, and distinctive weight ring channels impossible on conventional turning equipment. Nearly every Dif-e-Yo model featured removable rubber weight rings, giving players direct control over mass distribution and feel.
Dif-e-Yo's sponsored player Dave "Dazzling Dave" Schulte set the AYYA Eli Hop world record of 120 hops at the 2005 World Yo-Yo Championships using a Bare Bones, and received two signature models: the Bare Bones and InTernal Turmoil. Frank passed away unexpectedly on March 3, 2024 at Massachusetts General Hospital, age 71. In May 2024, Beyond YoYos released tribute versions of the Bare Bones and a new Bimetal Cross Bones as a memorial collaboration.

title: Dis
content: Dis is an independent yo-yo brand founded in 2023 by competitive player Remy Baskin of Northampton, Massachusetts. The brand produces limited-run precision throws that pair high-level performance with distinctive artistic packaging. Early releases have featured design collaborations with Martin Koprna of the Czech Republic and artwork by engravers and visual artists including In Hyeok Choi and Sean Thackeray. All Dis products are sold direct through the brand's website.

title: Diverse Animals
content:
Diverse Animals was founded on Earth. We feel that this is a great place to do business and the locals have been extremely warm and welcoming to our enterprises. We are committed to making quality throws with lots of love and bringing back the human touch that is so often lacking in the world of CNC.

Diverse Animals is committed to using both standard and nonstandard materials in our production. We are proud to say that we have experience with using metal, nonmetal, and tree in crafting our yo-yos. We have even gone to the expense of bringing the famed cinnamon blast into our brand’s possession by the inclusion of Patrick Condon as a team member.

We have a couple of yo-yos in the works that may be out for review soon. Keep your eyes open and receive them into your hearts. When they do start popping up for sale, remember that our runs are going to be small, indefinite, and sporadic. By that we mean this:

Diverse Animals are microbrewed with the finest flavors for the most discerning of palates. There is no set production number for any design. However, this does not apply to the gimmicks of special editions. Furthermore, we reserve the right to heckle you if you claim that you own a yo-yo of ours that is rare and one of some arbitrary number. These yo-yos are one of some, many, few, and a bunch. Diverse Animals are rare only so much as they are.

The production of every design we make is limited. Pat recently broke our time machine in an attempt to trade his potentially infinite resources for near-infinite amounts of dogs so we are no longer capable of producing infinite yo-yos. The unforeseeable volume of said dogs caused complications, and postponed Pat’s further plans to make every day Christmas. Any timetable for a release is probably a lie and should be treated as a teaser. Do not expect us to follow any sort of release pattern of other companies.

title: Doble
content: Doble Inc. was a small boutique American yo-yo manufacturer operated by John J. McAvoy Jr. The company specialized in premium handmade wooden fixed-axle and transaxle yo-yos featuring a proprietary adjustable string-gap mechanism — "lapper disc" technology — that let players fine-tune frictional drag via threaded knobs. McAvoy held three US patents covering the design.The Doble Calypso held a world record for fixed-axle sleep time at 63 seconds. The Titania, released in 1993, featured an innovative transaxle design where two freely-spinning halves allowed the player to grab the spinning yo-yo by its hubs — a concept predating modern hubstacks by nearly a decade. Doble operated quietly without major retail presence, with McAvoy crafting each yo-yo by hand. As late as 2007 the company was still producing yo-yos. The company is believed to have closed sometime in the late 2000s.

title: Doc Pop
content:
Doctor Popular (Doc Pop) is a San Francisco-based yo-yo player, artist, musician, and writer, known for pioneering styles including Moebius, Washing Machine, and Alpha style, as well as tricks such as the Gyroscopic Flop and the Schmoove Groove response system. He played for Team Anti-Yo and has had multiple signature yo-yos over the years, including the Super Scientist, Hesitator, Bolt, and Populist.

In 2006, Doc co-founded a yo-yo company called Yes, Absolutely with Phil Cox, releasing their first throw, The End. His current brand, Doc Pop Toys & Games, sells yo-yos (including the Bolt and The Populist — their first bi-metal), counterweights, enamel pins, and comics through doctorpopular.com. He also helped form the skill toy club College for the Easily Amused.

I initially had a throw away design idea i made for fun when Mark uploaded his video tutorials to YouTube. It was just for fun, designing an organic high wall that had a sort of stepped weight distro like a Cascade, but an under cut like the YWET. None of the proportions were right, and it sat for a while until I revisited the idea in 2022 after deciding to start a brand."

title: Dressel Designs
content:
Boutique yoyos designed by Patrick Dressel AKA Hobbygod.

Our design goals have always been to push the limits of design with unique and exciting yoyos at a really affordable price point.

title: Duncan Toys
content: Duncan® yo-yos are widely recognized as the finest yo-yos in the entire world. Since 1929, the name "Duncan" has been synonymous with "yo-yo."

title: Edition
content:
Edition is a boutique yo-yo brand founded in 2022 by a designer with prior involvement in OPYoyos. Their debut throw, the Reflection, was a bi-metal (6061 aluminum + stainless steel rings, 56mm diameter, 67g) released in a limited pre-order of 30 units, manufactured by FPM with CAD assistance from Alex Hattori. Edition went on to release additional models including the Aspen.

In 2025, Edition released their first monometal, the Forma — a 6061 aluminum throw inspired by mid-school designs (CLYW Chief, OneDrop Cascade, and the YYR x OneDrop SYFO). The Forma was prototyped across three shops (Lotaxi, FPM, and TopYo) before reaching its final form. Visit the Edition store or follow updates on the YoYoExpert Forums.

title: Elfverson & Co
content: Elfverson & Co AB of Påryd, Sweden is a wood-turning company. By its own account a predecessor began in 1874 and the business came into Elfverson family ownership in 1894. It makes the Kalmartrissan, a one-piece wooden yo-yo that its site says has been in production since 1932. The YoYo Wiki reports that Elfverson also made yo-yos for other brands, including Cheerio's Rainbow and Big Chief from 1958, as well as Royal, Festival and American Spinners.

title: Empathy
content: Empathy is an independent Czech yo-yo brand founded in 2022 by Tony Šec, a professional player based in Prague. The brand emerged from the Bohnice yo-yo scene — a tight-knit Czech community that has produced multiple European and World champions. Empathy designs are characterized by precise machining, refined weight placement, and a distinctly European aesthetic. The team spans Czech, Korean, British, and Ukrainian players. Each yo-yo reflects the player it is designed for rather than being a generic product.

title: Empress
content: Empress was a Japanese yo-yo brand of the early 1960s. The Yo-Yo Museum describes an Empress yo-yo from 1962 that copies the Duncan Satellite and is stamped "Japan". The YoYo Wiki lists a three-piece wooden Satellite and a plastic yo-yo under the name. Little is known about the company behind it.

title: en
content: en (エン) is a Japanese yo-yo brand whose official store gives a founding date of 1 January 2020. Its models take names from Japanese mythology, including the Amaterasu, Shinatsu and Tsuzure. Yo-Yo Store REWIND describes it as a domestic brand that releases yo-yos with an image character.

title: Enjoy Circle
content: Enjoy Circle is a Russian yo-yo company that YoYoExpert introduced as new, with the Aurus as its debut release. The Aurus is a bimetal with a 7075 aluminum body, stainless steel rings and an H-shaped profile. A forum thread links its release announcement to October 2024, and YoYoExpert's US listing followed in February 2025. Its founding year is unknown.

title: Enso
content:
Enso Yoyo is a yo-yo manufacturer dedicated to pushing the limits of design and materials. Founded in 2015, the company has built a reputation for bold engineering choices — from bimetal and tri-material constructions to exotic materials like Damascus steel and Grade 5 titanium. Their lineup spans budget-accessible throws to high-end collector pieces, united by a commitment to precision machining and distinctive aesthetics.

The team includes notable throwers Marc Zuno and Levi White, whose playing styles have influenced several product designs. Enso’s catalog includes the Damascus steel Full Metal Damascus, the ultra-wide Brolly and SSJ GOD MODE, the mini bimetal Gear 2, the tri-material Dragon Quest, and the One Drop Side Effect–compatible OG Bapehidora.

title: Eternal Throw
content: Eternal Throw was conceived on the drive home from the 2011 National Yo-Yo Contest by Chad Sage and Free Hinton — two Seattle-area fathers who had been throwing daily for more than a decade. Based in Seattle, WA, the brand built its identity around community: performing at Seattle Children's Hospital, Ronald McDonald House, local children's museums, and Boeing. Free Hinton maintained close ties with Rain City Skills, producing a co-branded beginner throw and fueling the brand's youth-outreach mission.Eternal Throw released infrequently — roughly one model every year or two — but each product was distinctive. The Victory was machined by One Drop and shipped with their Side Effect axle system. The Elysian placed 1st and 2nd at the 2014 Canadian Nationals before its public release. By their final era the brand had produced five models across six years. The YoYoExpert collection went dark circa 2019 with no formal closure announced.

title: EXPECTmake
content: EXPECTmake (企制®) is a Chinese yo-yo design studio founded by Renjie Lv, a former designer at Auldey — the large Chinese toy company behind a major line of professional-grade yo-yos. Lv launched EXPECTmake as an independent creative imprint focused on concept-driven, structurally ambitious design, operating as a design partner rather than a standalone manufacturer. All products are produced in collaboration with TOP YO under joint branding: "TOPYOnation® × 企制® (EXPECTmake)."The brand's debut, the Frozen (2021), established EXPECTmake's signature approach: removing material from the aluminum sidebody in a hollow hexagram pattern and filling the cavity with a clear polycarbonate "string shield" — preserving the visual effect while protecting the string. The design was recognized as one of the most thoughtfully executed hollow-structure bimetals in modern yo-yo making and was limited to approximately 100 units at $149.99. The Frozen II (2024) evolved the concept with tri-material A6061+stainless steel+polycarbonate construction, per-colorway unique CNC milling patterns, and a recessed center for finger spins.The Faceless (千面, 2024) shifted direction entirely — a modular polycarbonate design at $19.99 with interchangeable center pieces, broadening accessibility while retaining EXPECTmake's design-forward identity. The brand operates without a public website, distributing exclusively through TOP YO's retail network.

title: Fair Trade YoYos
content: Fair Trade YoYos is a brand whose FTY 138 YoYoExpert describes as an homage to its makers' punk-rock roots, named for the Misfits song "We Are 138". Retailers also list its Project Ti, in titanium, and the PV44. Its models are listed as designed in the USA and made in China. Its founder and founding year are unknown.

title: Fakies
content: Fakies was a short-lived American yo-yo brand active from 2001 to approximately 2003. The company produced a single model: a precision ball-bearing yo-yo molded to resemble a skateboard wheel, sold with licensed graphics from four real skateboard companies — Birdhouse, Blind, World Industries, and Speed Demons. The line comprised 24 distinct graphic variants.Yo-yo player Brian Cabildo (DXL Crew) assisted in developing the Fakies yo-yos from prototype to production. A Blind-branded variant is preserved in the collection of The Strong National Museum of Play in Rochester, NY (Object ID 108.3858).

title: Fallen44
content:
Fallen44 is a yo-yo company run by Kevin Markie, a woodworker and yo-yo enthusiast based in Charlotte, North Carolina. Founded around 2018, the idea behind Fallen44 was to create a horror-themed yo-yo company for fans of horror movie culture. Kevin handcrafts wooden fixed-axle yo-yos using a "vortex" response system and materials like spectra birch ply and maple. Product names are drawn from horror and supernatural themes.

Notable releases include the Sixth Sense (their first major retail release at YoYoExpert) and the 3AM. Fallen44 has also released collaborative pieces, including a 2019 World Yo-Yo Contest edition with YoYoSam made from ambrosia maple.

title: Featherspin Throws
content: Featherspin Throws is a merely a passion project born for the art of yoyoing. This is just a start, but if the way of the birds has taught us anything, it’s that every great journey begins with a single, powerful wingbeat.

title: Festival
content: Festival was a yo-yo brand owned by Wilfred Schlee Jr., who also owned Cheerio and Hi-Ker, according to the YoYo Wiki. The Yo-Yo Museum dates its Big Zapper to 1967-70 and the Smithsonian holds a Festival Screamer. The wiki gives the brand's span as the mid-1960s to the early 1980s, which is not independently confirmed, and lists models including the Big Zapper, Screamer, Zapper and a Sports Range of baseball, bowling-ball and football yo-yos. Elfverson of Sweden is documented as having made yo-yos for Festival.

title: Few & Far Between Yoyos
content: Few & Far Between Yoyos is a husband-and-wife boutique yoyo brand founded in October 2020 by Moises Vidal (forum handle: moefv) and his wife. The name reflects their philosophy of releasing small, exclusive runs of high-quality throws rather than mass-producing. Every model ships with premium packaging and custom accessories — matching strings, silk pouches, enamel pins, stickers, and spinning tops. Key design collaborators include Patrick Dressel (Dressel Designs) and artist Celen Garcia-Vidal. The brand built a dedicated following through their manufacturer thread on YoYoExpert forums. Their website went dark in 2024; the brand is considered inactive as of early 2025, though no formal closure announcement was made.

title: Flambeau
content: Flambeau, Inc. is a plastics manufacturer that says it was founded in 1947 in Bruce, Wisconsin and moved to Baraboo in 1950. It first worked in yo-yos as a contract maker of plastic yo-yos for Duncan, and its own history says it bought Duncan in 1968. The Smithsonian instead describes Duncan being auctioned in 1966, with Flambeau buying the name, so the transaction date is contested. Duncan has been a Flambeau division since.

title: Fli-Back
content: The Fli-Back Company, Inc. was a pioneering American yo-yo manufacturer based in High Point, North Carolina. Founded in 1931 as a paddleball manufacturer, the company expanded into yo-yos and spinning tops by 1946. At their peak in the 1950s, Fli-Back employed several hundred workers and sold products worldwide, becoming one of the most recognized yo-yo brands of the era.The company changed ownership from father to son in the early 1960s. Expansion plans were shelved in 1963, and in 1972 Fli-Back was sold to the Ohio Art Company, makers of the Etch-A-Sketch. The Hedstrom Company, the final owner, closed the North Carolina factory, moved production to Mississippi, and eventually discontinued all Fli-Back branded products in the early 1980s.

title: Flores Yo-Yo Company
content: The Flores Yo-Yo Company was founded in Santa Barbara, California in 1928 by Pedro Edralin Flores (1896–1964), a Filipino-American businessman credited with introducing the yo-yo to the United States market under that name. Flores's key innovation was looping the string around the axle rather than tying it, enabling the yo-yo to sleep freely and perform tricks — a departure from earlier fixed-string bandalores. At its peak in 1929, the enterprise operated three factories in Santa Barbara, Hollywood, and Los Angeles, employed 600 workers, and produced over 300,000 yo-yos daily before being acquired by Donald F. Duncan Sr. in 1932. Pedro Flores briefly revived the brand in 1954 under the Flores Corporation of America, but the original company name and trademark remained with Duncan.

title: Forester
content: Forester made a small line of wooden yo-yos in the 1960s, according to the YoYo Wiki, which lists the Worldsfair and Worldsfair Spinner. A collector publication spells the name "Forrester" and describes the World's Fair wooden yo-yos. The wiki notes the Worldsfair was not made for a World's Fair, though some dealers labelled it that way. The company's city and years are unknown.

title: ForYoSa
content: ForYoSa is a Taiwanese yo-yo brand founded in 2023 by Stephen Hung and based in Taichung. The name blends “Formosa,” the historical name for Taiwan, with “yo-yo.” Its first release was the Stinky Tofu, a 7075 aluminum butterfly-shaped unresponsive yo-yo, in September 2023, followed by the CNC polycarbonate Crystal Dumpling in 2024. The brand also distributes free 3D-printable designs and accessories.

title: Franklin Mint
content: The Franklin Mint is an American collectibles company founded in 1964 by Joseph Segel in Wawa, Pennsylvania. It built its reputation manufacturing and marketing limited-edition commemorative coins, medals, jewelry, die-cast vehicle replicas, porcelain figurines, and luxury dolls.In 1994 Franklin Mint extended their collectibles model to yo-yos, licensing a planned 12-piece subscription series of historically significant Duncan yo-yo reproductions. Due to poor initial sales, only three of the twelve planned models were produced. The series — reproductions of the Duncan Litening, Duncan Imperial, and the Large "G" Genuine Duncan — are now sought after by collectors precisely because of their rarity. Each came with a gold-finished engraved metal display stand.

title: Free2Throw
content: Free2Throw was founded by Tony Saffioti, according to YoYoExpert, to make unique and affordable yo-yos for all levels. Its first design was the LiV, a bimetal named after Alpha 5 of Power Rangers. Retailers list it as designed in the USA and made in China. Its founding year and status are unverified.

title: Freshly Dirty
content: Freshly Dirty got its start in summer of 2016 when Alex Morton started experimenting with making fixed axle yo-yos using a dress press on his back porch in Greenwood, Indiana. It expanded in scope in August of 2016 when Alex and I met at the World Yo-yo Contest in Cleveland and decided to take on the project of making a metal yo-yo together. I had some previous with yo-yo design and manufacturing when I started a brand called Kingspin back in 2010-2011. From 2016 on, we consistently released a few yo-yos each year and build a small following. Around 2019, development of the Mod44 started, which gained us a lot of exposure and carved a niche out for us to continue to innovate with modular design in yo-yo and push the envelope with ambitious designs. We continued this trend in 2024 with the Stem system, further pushing into configurability as an area of expertise in yo-yo design.

title: Freshthings
content: FRESHTHINGS is a Japanese yo-yo and lifestyle brand directed by World Yo-Yo Champion Hiroyuki Suzuki (also founder of sOMEThING). Launched November 2, 2016, the brand pursues an explicitly crossover identity — releasing yo-yos in collaboration with streetwear labels, beverage brands, sports teams, artists, and hotels rather than the competitive circuit. Collaborators include fragment design, Coca-Cola, A BATHING APE, Mark Gonzales, Medicom Toy, and others. Hardware is produced using platforms ranging from classic plastic loop shapes to machined aluminum and titanium performance bodies.

title: G Squared Yoyos
content:
G-Squared, or G2, began in 2012 by Jacob Gross. Please visit G2 online, or join the G2 Nation group on Facebook to learn more.
