title: Gates YoYo
content: Gates YoYo is a one-man, hand-machined yo-yo and spin top workshop founded in 2017 by Jon Gates out of Aurora, Colorado. Every yo-yo half is individually turned on a lathe without jigs or molds, meaning no two units are exactly alike. Gates began yo-yoing in 1976, went pro in 1990, founded the Denver Yo-Yo Club in 1998, and is widely credited as the creator of the offstring bind that gave rise to the 4A division. In 2020 he was inducted into the US National Yo-Yo Hall of Fame. His catalog spans fixed-axle laminated-wood throws and bearing-equipped unresponsive wooden yo-yos, all built to competition-level smoothness.

title: General-Yo
content: General-Yo was founded in the second half of 2008 by Ernie Kaiser, an aerospace engineer based in Riverside, California. After rekindling his passion for yoyoing following a 25-year break, Kaiser applied his aerospace machining expertise to produce high-precision, American-made metal yoyos. The company's debut throw — the Torrent — immediately established General-Yo's reputation for uncompromising quality.All General-Yo yoyos are machined to extreme tolerances, with Ernie personally rejecting units for wobble or anodizing defects. The brand is known for their proprietary HAT-PAD response system, AIGR (Aircraft Instrument Grade Rated) bearings, and ultra-limited production runs — most models number in the dozens to low hundreds of units. General-Yo has explored nearly every material class: 6061 and 7075 aluminum, 7075 bimetal with stainless steel and brass rings, and a legendary magnesium throw (the Magnum). The brand celebrated its 10th anniversary in 2018 and continues producing new models as of 2025.

title: God-Tricks
content: God-Tricks was founded in August 2010 in Shenzhen, China by Wang Zhan Hong (Jeyo), a seven-year yoyo veteran dedicated to producing professional-grade yoyos at accessible price points. Launching with the Destiny — a full-aluminum 1A throw priced under $35 — the company quickly gained international recognition for delivering competition-capable performance at prices that undercut established Western brands.God-Tricks later launched a premium sub-label, GT·INFINITY (Infiniti GT), for more technically ambitious designs including bimetal and titanium constructions. At its peak the brand sponsored competitions across China, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia, and Slovakia, distributing products in over ten countries. The product line grew to more than 25 models across 1A, 3A, 4A, and 5A play styles. God-Tricks appears to have wound down around 2019–2020; the website remains online but static.

title: Goody Manufacturing Company
content: The Goody Manufacturing Company was a New York City–based toy maker and one of the primary competitors of the Duncan Toys Company during the 1940s and 1950s. Because Duncan had trademarked the term “yo-yo,” Goody marketed their products as “Filipino Twirlers,” a nod to the toy’s presumed Filipino origins. The company distinguished itself with unusually ornate wooden models decorated with colorful painted stripes and rhinestones of varying colors — a hallmark made distinctive by Goody’s practice of drilling jewel holes after painting, leaving a ring of bare wood around each stone.

title: Gorham Manufacturing Company
content: Gorham Manufacturing Company was one of the largest and most prestigious American sterling silver manufacturers, founded in Providence, Rhode Island in 1831 by Jabez Gorham. Best known for flatware and hollowware, Gorham also produced sterling silver yo-yos as luxury gift items across multiple production eras from approximately the 1910s through the 1970s. Their yo-yos feature a sterling silver (925) shell over a weighted steel body and are held in museum collections including the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History and the RISD Museum. The Providence manufacturing plant closed in 1986. The Gorham brand is currently owned by Lifetime Brands, Inc.

title: Gropper Mfg
content: The YoYo Wiki identifies Gropper Mfg. Co., Inc. as a Brooklyn, New York toy maker that began making toys in the 1920s and produced yo-yos and tops in the 1950s and 1960s. Its yo-yo was the Up-N-Down, made in several versions. Toy-industry directories list more than one Gropper company in New York, so the exact maker and dates are unverified.

title: GWAY Throws
content:
GWAY Throws — short for Guy With A YoYo — is a boutique yoyo brand run by Sean Collins, a well-known personality on the YoYoExpert Forums and YouTube. GWAY makes high-quality aluminum throws known for their unique aesthetics, sleek packaging, and collaborative designs.

Notable releases include the Daredevil (their first retail release), the Saboteur (an organic design developed in collaboration with Anomaly Yo-Yo's), the Regulator (co-designed with Dressel Designs), and the GEEDORAH (a competition-focused double-rim design also co-designed with Sean Collins — the 5th release from the brand).

If you have additional info on the Released/Retired dates, please email us at [email removed].

title: Heaven Sent
content: Heaven Sent was a short-lived streetwear-inflected yo-yo label launched in 2016 as a sub-brand of Canadian return-top maker CLYW (Caribou Lodge Yo-Yo Works). Created and directed by Alec Campbell — CLYW's in-house photographer/videographer — with CLYW manufacturing and distributing, the label drew visual inspiration from streetwear and lookbook-style photography rather than typical yo-yo marketing. Its sole yo-yo release, the Creep, sold alongside apparel through the brand's own online store (heavensent.rip). No formal closure was ever announced; a final documented run of the Creep is reported as late as September 2022, per forum accounts (unconfirmed official record).

title: Henrys
content: Henrys GmbH is a juggling equipment manufacturer and distributor based in Karlsruhe, Germany, founded in 1984. The company began producing yo-yos in the late 1990s, starting with the Viper — a large-diameter aluminum-hubbed yo-yo designed for stage visibility that became a pioneer of offstring (4A) play. Their AXYS interchangeable axle system, introduced in 1999, allowed players to swap between fixed, transaxle, and ball bearing configurations across the entire product line. Henrys manufactures all products in-house in their Karlsruhe factory.

title: Hesh Enterprises
content: Hesh Enterprises is a sole proprietorship of Brendan McGinnis in the San Francisco Bay Area. By its own account it began in 2018 with the Petri, which he designed and manufactured while working at a machine shop in San Carlos, California. Later designs are made by One Drop Yo-yos in Eugene, Oregon, and the second model is the Honeypot. McGinnis has been a professional player for Caribou Lodge since 2020.

title: HICOO
content:
HICOO was a small artisan yo-yo manufacturer founded in 2006 by designer Shu-Yu Chen (known in the community as “Black Cement”) and partner Lucifer Chen. Based in mainland China, the brand holds a landmark place in yo-yo history as the creator of the first high-end aluminum yo-yo ever produced by a Chinese manufacturer.

The debut model, the West Uranium, was deliberately priced low so that players in mainland China could experience premium metal construction for the first time. Black Cement’s background in visual design was evident throughout the product line: every model featured distinctive engravings, considered aesthetics, and precision machining that punched far above the brand’s low profile.

HICOO collaborated twice with Auldey Toys — one of China’s largest toy manufacturers — producing the Virus and a collab version of the Inca, giving both products wider distribution. The brand was active for approximately three years, releasing around eight distinct yo-yo designs before going quiet in the late 2000s. All HICOO models are now considered rare collector pieces.

title: Holgate Toy Company
content: Holgate Toy Company was a wooden toy maker in Kane, Pennsylvania, with woodworking roots going back to 1789 and toy production from 1929. The YoYo Wiki lists yo-yos in eight shapes: Triangle, Square, Octagon, Heptagon, Flower, Shamrock, Star and Heart. A patent catalog lists four Holgate design patents, so the claim that all eight shapes were patented is unverified. Its current status is unknown.

title: HSpin
content: HSpin Yo-Yo LLC (stylized HSPIN) is a Swiss precision yo-yo manufacturer founded in 1997 by Christopher Kayatz, who designed the prototype HandQuake 1.3 while on an ABB internship, teaching himself AutoCAD on the company's CNC equipment. The brand began with students assembling yo-yos in Zurich dorm rooms and carrying boxes by tram to the post office.HSpin pioneered several foundational innovations in modern yo-yo design: the bi-metal yo-yo (HandQuake 1.4, 1998, the first yo-yo with embedded steel weight rings), stock recessed friction sticker response on aluminum (G&E2, 2004), profile laser engraving (Pyro, 2005), and the H-shaped rim-weight profile (Envy, 2007) that influenced an entire generation of competition yo-yos. Manufacturing partnerships with Florian and Paul in Bremgarten, Switzerland date to 2007. HSpin operated until December 2013, then relaunched in January 2024 with the Handquake 2.

title: Huatian
content: Huatian is a Chinese yo-yo brand focused on building throws that are interesting, unique, and fun rather than purely streamlined for competition. Its lineup ranges from casual everyday models like the Holiday to flagship mono- and bi-metal designs such as the Pinecone RE and Banshee.

title: Hubless Yoyo
content: Hubless Yoyo is a small American yo-yo maker, per the company's own site (archived) based in Long Beach, California, founded 2014. Debut and signature release is the Doughnut, the first production hubless (hollow-center) yo-yo, launched Thanksgiving Day, November 23, 2017 — confirmed via YoYo Museum exhibit record. A 'Doughnut Bite Size' variant followed.Unverified as of Aug 2026: company site (hublessyoyo.com) unreachable during research, founding year/Long Beach location sourced only to an archived (Wayback) company page rather than a live source, and current operating status could not be confirmed — no evidence of formal closure but no evidence of continued activity either. Social links below could not be independently confirmed as currently owned by the company and are left blank pending verification.

title: Hummingbird Toy Company, Ltd.
content: Hummingbird Toy Company, Ltd. was a wooden yo-yo manufacturer founded in 1982 by furniture maker Brad Countryman in Arcade, New York. Starting from a woodshop using scrap materials, Hummingbird quickly gained attention for high-end, handcrafted wooden yo-yos. The company's first commercial run of 10,000 units caught the eye of major retailers including L.L. Bean, Eddie Bauer, and Land's End, establishing Hummingbird as an internationally known brand by the late 1980s.Known for multi-layer laminated dyed wood construction and meticulous craftsmanship, Hummingbird yo-yos became favorites among competitive players including Dale Myrberg, Jennifer Baybrook, and Dennis McBride. The company faced significant challenges in 1989 when a severe flood damaged the factory. Despite recovery efforts, business decisions and manufacturing shifts led to a transition away from yo-yo production by the early 1990s. The company eventually closed in 1995 after moving manufacturing operations to China, shifting focus to wooden railway sets and other products.Today, vintage Hummingbird yo-yos remain highly collectible pieces of yo-yo history, prized for their wooden construction, elegant design, and association with the sport's golden age.

title: Humphrey Corporation
content: Humphrey Corporation was founded in the early 1970s by brothers Dave and Ken Humphrey, initially producing the Humphrey Flyer frisbee as an advertising promotional item. In 1975 the company expanded into yo-yos, and by the 1980s and 1990s had become one of the largest producers of promotional yo-yos in the United States, manufacturing over 1,000 distinct branded variants per year and more than one million total units. The company sold exclusively through a distributor network — never direct to retail consumers — supplying customized yo-yos to corporations and small businesses as branded giveaways. In later years production consolidated around a single mold, the All Pro, a shape now known among collectors as "the Humphrey style."

title: Hydrangea
content: Hydrangea is a Japanese yo-yo brand known for high-performance titanium and aluminum models. Founded around 2020, the company produces competition-grade yo-yos with a focus on balance and precision.

title: ikimono
content: ikimono is a small-batch indie yo-yo project founded by Josef Chung, publicly announced on National Yo-Yo Day (June 6, 2022) after over a year of private prototyping. The brand released a single model, the Tomo, in August 2024 — an undersized 7075 aluminum monometal with machined acrylic accent rings, priced at $99. The launch and a limited engraved collaboration edition with Unknown (the brand founded by six-time National Yo-Yo Champion Bryan Figueroa) both sold out quickly and are sought after by collectors. As of its own Instagram bio the brand is on hiatus, and its website has since gone offline.Headquarters location is unconfirmed: the brand's website backend was configured for Japan/Tokyo, but at least one retailer listed the Tomo as "Designed in the United States."

title: ilinx Toys
content:
ilinx Toys (doing business as Hollywood Modern Yoyos) is an independent yoyo brand based in Hollywood, California, founded by Ross Levine. The company focuses on thoughtful, theory-driven design—prioritizing flow-arts playability, off-axis capability, and everyday carry—over competition-spec conformity. ilinx is also the home of the Kill Your Yoyo podcast, a bi-weekly conversation series about yoyo improvisation and theory. The brand produces aluminum monogetals, 3D-printed yoyos, and its own line of slim response pads.

Its yo-yos, pads and bearings are also sold through modernyoyos.com under the Hollywood Modern Yoyos name.

title: ILYY
content: ILYY (formally ILOVEYOYO) was founded in August 2006 by raytsh and crackout. The main idea behind this project was to create a yo-yo for themselves that would meet the preferences of both of them. This then developed into a yo-yo manufacturer that sells internationally.

title: Imperial Toy Company
content: Imperial Toy Company was a US toy maker, listed with a 1969 founding date, that became known for low-priced yo-yos alongside marbles and bubble soap, according to the YoYo Wiki. Many of its plastic yo-yos carry a crown mark, and the company is unrelated to Duncan's Imperial model. Ja-Ru states that it acquired Imperial in 2019. The YoYo Wiki lists models including Candy Club, Champion, Giant Teeny, Hi-Tech, Hot Wheels, Super Stock and Teeny.

title: Infinite Illusions
content: Infinite Illusions, operating online as YoYoGuy.com, was the first major online yoyo retailer and for many years the largest in the US. Founded by Greg Cohen in Tallahassee, Florida in 1986 as a juggling equipment company, the shop expanded into yoyos in 1989 and launched YoYoGuy.com in the late 1990s. The company hosted the World Yo-Yo Contest in Orlando from 2000 through 2013, growing from 315 to roughly 900 participants before the IYYF took over in 2014.

title: Ioiô Fênix
content: Ioiô Fênix (Portuguese: "Phoenix Yo-Yo") is the leading manufacturer of plastic yo-yos in Latin America, founded in Brazil around 2008 and based in Arujá, São Paulo. The company produces entry-level through professional-grade yo-yos and sponsors promotional events and school yo-yo campaigns throughout Brazil. In 2011–2012, Fênix launched Brazilian Yoyo as its high-end aluminum competition division, releasing machined throws that reached international markets. The company also produces spinning tops under the Fênix brand and has collaborated with Brazilian street artist and yo-yo player Titi Freak on limited-edition colorways.

title: iYoYo
content: iYoYo is a German yo-yo brand founded in 2015 by Dave Geigle — 5× European YoYo Championship Champion and multiple German National Champion. Known for collaborations with designer Ze'ev Yehuda, player signatures (Ryan Connolly, Mathilde Witt), and brand collabs with ILYY, YoYoFactory, YoYoTricks, hspin, and CLYW, iYoYo spans beginner aluminum models through competition titanium bimetals. The brand operates alongside yo-shop.de, Germany's long-running specialty yo-yo retailer.

title: Ja-Ru
content: Ja-Ru, Inc. is a toy company based in Jacksonville, Florida, which says on its own site that it was founded in 1961 and acquired Imperial Toy in 2019. The YoYo Wiki lists a number of Ja-Ru yo-yo lines, including the All Star, American Champ, Today's Toys, Super Sports Festival and Stunt Wheelie, and notes that the name is not an abbreviation of "Jack Russell", as some collectors believed. Dates for its yo-yo production are not established.

title: Jake Bullock
content:
From Jake:

"I’ve been yoyoing since 2003. I was a part of Team Anti-Yo from 2006-2009. I never won any major contests but I placed 2nd a lot during my short competitive career (06-08). I won Trick Innovator of the Year alongside Jon Rob for our 5A efforts in 2007. I fell out of the yoyo scene from 2010-2015 but I never stopped yoyoing. In 2016 I came back because Worlds was in Cleveland relatively close to my home for the first time. I reconnected with a lot of old friends. After Worlds 2019 I created my yo-yo instagram (@jakebullockyoyo) and shortly after that decided to try my hand at making the signature yo-yo I never got back in my heyday. My friend Tyler Severance put me in touch with a factory and his designer, CJ Atkinson, and in the midst of the pandemic of 2020 the Dunk was born.

What started as a one-off project that I wasn’t sure would succeed has grown into an entire line of different yo-yos and accessories. I get an immense amount of joy and satisfaction from playing with my own yo-yo and seeing other people all over the world collect and enjoy them. It’s the definition of a dream come true for me."

title: Japan Looping Solutions
content: Japan Looping Solutions is based in Minokamo, Gifu, a well-known 2A (looping) hotbed. Looping players there began developing their own yo-yo because few options existed, and its official site says the first prototype took a month and the official release about two years. Its product is the LoopUp, which Yo-Yo Store REWIND shows on sale from December 2017. Sponsored players won 2A at the 2018 and 2019 Japan Nationals and the 2019 World Yo-Yo Contest.

title: Japan Technology
content: Japan Technology is a yo-yo manufacturer founded in 2009 by Atsushi Yamada in Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan, initially specializing in precision-machined Delrin offstring yo-yos for professional 4A competition. The company's debut model, the Kamui, was revolutionary for being machined from a single block of Delrin — unlike the molded plastic competitors of its era — and established JT as the premier name in high-end offstring design. Over the following decade and a half, JT expanded into string trick aluminum and titanium monometals, bimetals, and a wide range of plastic designs, while maintaining a core identity in performance-driven, competition-grade offstring engineering.

title: JIGUN
content: JIGUN is a competition-focused yo-yo brand operating under Lab Exploration Program (LEP), based in Kanagawa, Japan with ties to China's competitive scene. The brand is known for signature throws for Chinese champions Wu Congcong and Luckey Yulin Li, as well as Zhang Suze, spanning aluminum, bimetal, tri-material, titanium, and magnesium construction. JIGUN also collaborates with accessory brand Sochi Company on premium limited-edition models.

title: July YoYo
content: July YoYo is a Chinese independent yo-yo brand founded around 2020 by MaFeng, known for competitive-grade throws at accessible price points. Their budget monometal Sharpness became one of the best-selling entry-level metal yo-yos in China. The brand distributes globally through specialty retailers including Yo-Yo Store Rewind and YoYoExpert, and has collaborated multiple times with Taiwanese manufacturer TopYo on the Overlap 7068, Reality, and Null. The lineup spans budget monometals, polycarbonate bimaterials, and premium titanium-rim flagship throws.

title: KenTech
content: KenTech is a micro yo-yo brand founded in 2015 by Ken Luo, a mechanical engineering student from Washington state and the 2015 PNWR (Pacific NorthWest Regional) 3A division champion. The brand launched with a single product — the Euler, a compact bimetal with stainless steel rims — that made an outsized impression for its technical performance and exceptionally low body weight. Ken's engineering background drove a design philosophy of simple shape with maximum performance, stripping unnecessary aesthetic elements in favor of pure function.At launch, KenTech ran an unusual "Technology For Champions" incentive program: any US National Champion who won using a KenTech yo-yo would receive $500, and any World Champion would receive $1,000. Despite the strong debut, the brand went dormant after the initial Euler run sold through, with no subsequent original releases.In 2018, the Euler design resurfaced through a collaboration with Japanese distributor Yoku YoYo Design, distributed by Yo-Yo Store REWIND, at a more accessible $69.99 price point with multiple splash colorways. KenTech has no website or social media presence; all known products have sold through with no restocks.

title: King Yo Star
content: King Yo Star (KYS) was founded in 2011 as a dual-entity operation between Vancouver, BC, Canada and China. Established by Jeremy McKay ("Mr. Yoyothrower") and the KYS Design Team — Steven Vong Kin Ian and Kuyos Chen Jia Lin — the company built its early identity around yoyos where width exceeds diameter, anti-vibration ring technology, and extra-wide catch zones.The lineup expanded from the aluminum 2011 debut models through bi-metal innovation with the Rapid (2014) — designed with 2013 US 5A National Champion Jake Elliott — and a 4A collaboration with MonkeyfingeR Design on the Silverback King (2016). KYS was active through approximately 2017.

title: Kusan
content: Kusan Inc. was a Nashville, Tennessee manufacturer that made plastic yo-yos in the 1950s and 1960s, according to the YoYo Wiki and a retailer listing. The Yo-Yo Museum identifies its Twin Twirler, a yo-yo and top combination, from around 1953. Founding and closure years are unknown.

title: Kyo
content: Kyo is a small-batch precision yo-yo manufacturer operated by Kyle Weems, a machinist, modder, and mechanical engineering graduate from Florida State University. Weems discovered yo-yos through a 1998 school science project and spent years combining his passion for the hobby with his manufacturing expertise, eventually building a brand known for uncompromising metallurgy and ultra-limited production runs. The Kyo name first appeared in 2004 with the Immortalis, a machined aluminum butterfly sold exclusively through Infinite Illusions.Over two decades, Kyo released fewer than fifteen production models — each a distinct engineering milestone. The Phi (2005) introduced reversible spacers and inner rim grinds derived from the golden ratio; the TiPhiter (c. 2006) was only the second titanium yo-yo ever commercially produced; the Alph (2006) became the first 7075-aluminum Kyo model; and the Death Robot Mg (2016) broke new ground as the world's first magnesium and dual stainless-steel bi-metal. In 2018 the Tinman arrived as the first diamond-coated titanium yo-yo in the hobby's history.Beyond production throws, Kyle Weems has served as a contract machinist for larger brands — notably designing the Duncan Vendetta (2009) — and pioneered a custom yo-yo design service using 3D printing and lathe finishing. Kyo remains a one-person operation with production measured in dozens per model.

title: Laid Back Swing
content: Laid Back Swing is a Japanese yo-yo brand that launched in December 2022. Its stated aim is to make yo-yos for adults who love different cultures, for competition, casual play, collecting and art. Its flagship Authentic was followed by the Nude Trump, which converts between bind and responsive.

title: Lathed Back Design
content: Founded in 2019 by a husband-and-wife team in Calgary, Alberta, Canada, Lathed Back Design is a skill toy company specializing in titanium yo-yos and handcrafted skill toys. Shortly after founding, a house fire took nearly everything from them — but they rebuilt, relaunched, and channeled that experience into their guiding mission: creating objects that can bring joy even at the darkest point.Every yo-yo is designed, tested, and finished in-house. All anodizing is done one piece at a time, producing unique splash patterns, etch effects, and custom finishes unavailable elsewhere. The company is best known for their modular titanium system, which lets a single core yo-yo transform across multiple play styles and configurations via interchangeable rim sets — bridging fixed-axle, responsive, and unresponsive play in one compact package.

title: Layer Infinity
content:
From Wayne at Layer Infinity:

"During the COVID pandemic I picked up 3D printing as a hobby. I've been playing return tops for 20+ish years, and with the new hobby on top I started having ideas on what I can make.As I posted some of my stuff in my personal instagram @wayne927, many people have asked me if I will share the source models or just buy the prints from me.

So, here it is. I'll put up some of my stuff on this site over time. You can also follow the brand instagram @layerinfinity or Facebook page @layerinfinity to see what's coming. If something is posted there, it will be available either for sale or for free download. I will continue posting my own stuff in my personal account, and you're welcome to contact me if you're interested in the ones that are not on this site.

Everything by Layer Infinity is made in my bedroom at home, in Toronto Canada."

title: LEAD
content: LEAD is a competitive yo-yo brand based in Shanghai, China. Founded by a Chinese national yo-yo champion — known in the community as one of China's foremost competitive players — the brand launched its first product, the Protagonist bimetal, in 2025. LEAD debuted internationally through the yoyobox store and gained rapid attention in competitive circles for precise engineering and clean design.The brand targets the high-performance competition market, releasing precision bimetal and monometal designs at accessible price points. All products have sold out at launch. The brand's official online store opened in May 2026.

title: Lab Exploration Program
content: Lab Exploration Program (LEP) is a yo-yo brand based in Kanagawa, Japan, with operations spanning Japan and China. The brand launched in 2021 with the ONIGOKKO, a signature model for Chinese national champion Wu Congcong, and established itself in the competitive scene through technically ambitious designs and close collaboration with top international players.LEP operates under two lines: the primary LEP brand and the JIGUN sub-brand, which covers the full range from entry-level plastic throws to ultra-premium titanium and magnesium models. The brand is known for innovations including tri-material constructions (aluminum + polycarbonate + titanium or stainless steel rings), patented POM rim designs (New Moon), the YOFO hybrid yo-yo/spin-top, and the KAWA off-string yo-yo. All products are sold through LEP's Shopify storefront at labexplorationprogram.com. Key signature players include Wu Congcong (Chinese national champion), Hu Congcong (Chinese champion), Wayne Chung Cheng Hsun (9-time Taiwan champion), Yulin Li "Luckey" (multi-national champion), and Zhang Suze.

title: L.H. Knibb Co.
content: L.H. Knibb Co. was founded by the inventor Leroy Hayes Knibb, according to the YoYo Wiki. A collector chronology dates its Dyna-Glo glowing yo-yo to 1952. The company's city, founding and closure are unknown.

title: Luftverk
content:
From Jeffrey Pang:

"I started making titanium yoyos as a machining challenge while studying engineering. I got into yoyos as a kid in 2005 after watching a video of Japan Nationals my cousin sent me, and as a restless fidgety 13 year old - I was hooked. As I got older my interest in the little toy dropped a bit but after I built a 3d printer in my university years, I decided to design and print a yoyo to some degree of success. A few friends wanted them, so I sold them on a simple website. After a while with the influence of the community, I created and released the full titanium Evora which sold out 50 units in under a minute. It was nuts. What was originally a one time release became the brand Luftverk - yet I never expected it to grow to what it is today. Fast forward 6 years later and releases are still happening and the fan base keeps growing larger than I ever imagined.⁣ I still do limited releases (although not as often) and I generally will only do ideas that I am genuinely interested in, regardless of what the rest of the industry is up to. This is possible because of the customers who believe in my designs and products. This really is more of an art than a science and I try not to forget that.⁣I am lucky to have the support from people all over the world and have opportunities to share my passion for design, photography and the unique properties of titanium. If you are reading this then you are on the new post 2020 website - but to preserve the original unedited information, here is the much longer story I wrote on the old website 5 years ago of how Luftverk came into existence.⁣"

title: Lumar
content:
Lumar was the British yo-yo brand of Louis Marx and Company, the American toy mogul who built one of the world’s largest toy empires from the 1920s onward. Marx began manufacturing tin yo-yos in England under the Lumar name around 1930, operating first from Dudley before establishing a factory in Swansea, Wales by the late 1940s. The name “Lumar” was a contraction of Louis Marx’s own name, used exclusively for his British market toy lines, which also included tin trains, vehicles, and toy gramophones.

A private arrangement between Louis Marx and his friend Donald Duncan shaped Lumar’s market for decades: in exchange for Marx keeping Lumar out of the American yo-yo trade, Duncan paid Marx a commission on his New York-area sales. The gentleman’s agreement left Lumar as the definitive British yo-yo brand through the postwar era. Over the 1950s through 1970s the line moved from all-tin construction into wooden and plastic models, producing a full range from beginner-grade models to competition-branded “Championship 99” yo-yos, as well as licensed character yo-yos (The Wombles, The Muppet Show) and specialty variants including a Whistling Yo-yo and butterfly-shaped models.

In 1967 Dunbee-Combex acquired both Louis Marx and Co. Ltd. and Lumar Ltd. as part of a consolidation of the Marx UK operations; after Quaker Oats divested the US Marx division in 1976 the Swansea factory continued under new ownership until financial losses forced its permanent closure in 1981. Lumar yo-yos are now sought-after British vintage collectibles, with early tin Beginners models and the single surviving Jewel 99 prototype — found in the shuttered Swansea factory by a collector — among the most prized examples.

title: MadHouse YoYos
content: MadHouse YoYos was a small-batch American yo-yo manufacturer founded in 2008 by Rick Kroytz in California's San Joaquin Valley, later operating out of Central Oregon. The company focused on distinctive, visually striking throws with unconventional finishes and unusual design choices, including a patented fusion color-bonding process and a large hubstack system they called "TA-Ta." Their six-model catalog, released between 2008 and 2013, attracted a cult following for combining high-end performance with eye-catching aesthetics. All known models are discontinued, and the brand appears to have been inactive since approximately 2013.

title: MagicYoYo
content: About MagicYoYoMagicYoYo (GT Int Group – TND Toys) was founded in 2004 in Shenzhen, China and became one of the most widely recognized names in the global yo-yo market by offering precision-machined aluminum and bi-metal throws at a fraction of the price of comparable Western brands. The company built its reputation on the N-series, T-series, and K-series models of the early 2010s — particularly the N5 Desperado, N12 Shark Honor, and T5 Overlord — which introduced thousands of players to unresponsive metal yo-yos. Over the following decade MagicYoYo expanded into every segment: dedicated looping (D-series), beginner plastics (K-series), LED models, finger spin platforms (V-series), bi-metals, titanium throws, and internationally notable collaborations including the SKYVA with Jeffrey Pang of Luftverk and the Katana series with Japanese retailer SpinGear. Their store operates at gomagicyoyo.com.

title: Markmont.
content: Markmont. is the independent skill toy brand of Mark Montgomery, 2003 AP World Yo-Yo Champion and longtime figure in the yo-yo community. Mark has been involved in the sport since 1996 and was previously sponsored by Duncan, Yomega, Buzz-On, and One Drop Design.All Markmont. aluminum throws are machined in collaboration with One Drop Design in Eugene, Oregon. The brand also produces hand-twisted yo-yo string under the Markmont. Formulas label and small-batch roasted coffee (Markmont. Joe).Mark studied graphic design and animation at the Savannah College of Art and Design and worked at Adult Swim. His design philosophy blends classic organic shapes with modern performance — most fully expressed in the Markmont. Classic, which went through twelve prototype drawings and six physical builds before release.

title: Matt Schmidt YoYos
content:
Matt Schmidt created the Underdog yo-yos.

Matt was a well known fixture in the St. Paul/Minneapolis yo-yo community. He regularly competed in MWR and the Minnesota State yo-yo contest. He also judged at MWR and MN State a few times.

Sadly, Matt passed away March 13, 2019.

title: Medalist
content: Medalist was a yo-yo line distributed by Strombeck Mfg. Co. According to the Yo-Yo Museum, Strombeck bought 22 of Duncan's lathes at the June 1966 liquidation and sold yo-yos under the Medalist name. The museum documents the Cadet, Trickmaster and Trophy. The YoYo Wiki says the line sold poorly without the Duncan brand and ran only a short time.

title: Mike Monty Yoyos
content: Mike Monty Yoyos is the personal yo-yo brand of Emmett, Idaho player, designer, maker, and teacher Michael “MikeMonty” Montgomery. Montgomery began designing and manufacturing yo-yos through Double-Take Industries around 2010, followed by Montgomery Yo-Yo Company and the 2012 Tinder release, then Burgeon Yo-Yos and its handmade Roots fixed-axle model in 2017.The MikeMonty name became a yo-yo brand in 2019 with Cambium, a small-batch wooden fixed-axle design. The aluminum Memento followed in 2020, while the convertible GLHF and performance-focused Mori arrived in 2021. Montgomery also helped design the 2013 MonkeyfingeR Design Forte, his signature model. His catalog spans handmade wood yo-yos, beginner-friendly convertible throws, and modern aluminum designs.

title: Mile High Yoyo Club
content: Mile High Yoyo Club is a small-batch yoyo brand and community club based in the Denver/Littleton, Colorado area — "Mile High" for Colorado's elevation. Founded in 2022 by Dave (forum handle: bobafret) after a conversation during his recovery from a heel injury, the brand's entire run is built around a single aluminum mold — The Gnome — released in a series of limited-edition colorway drops, each sold through Instagram DMs and at local club meets at PlayForge Games and The Rabbit Hole Café. A final product, the Mile Highbrid (POM + aluminum hybrid), closed out the brand in late 2025. The club hosts bimonthly meetups in the Denver metro area.

title: Mister Babache
content: Mister Babache is a Swiss juggling-equipment brand, best known for diabolos, sold today through the Jonglerie shop. Its official history dates the Mister Babache brand to 1990, within the Jonglerie Diffusion business that began in 1985. The YoYo Wiki says it produced its own yo-yos at one point, listing the Yoyoyo, Yoyowl and Yoyogi, though only some of these are corroborated.

title: MK1 YoYos
content:
MK1 Yoyos is a US-based yoyo company founded in 2018 by Mark Diehr. The brand focuses on experimental and innovative aspects of yoyo design. Mark's first release, the Diffraction, had a very limited run, but the updated Diffraction v2 helped establish MK1 as a serious boutique brand. MK1 is known for pushing creative boundaries, from slimline designs to tri-material collaborations.

Notable releases include the Heron (a collaboration with Yoyofriends featuring 7075 aluminum, stainless steel rings, and a polycarbonate outer ring), the Ring-Bearer (a Lord of the Rings collaboration), the Laze, and the Exia.

meta.yya_company_profile:
How did the idea for MK1 come about?

I was learning how to design yoyos for fun, and Jordan Blofeld (Smashing yoyos, OP Yoyos) challenged me to make something that people wanted to buy. That ended up being the Diffraction.

I created the MK1 branding to make it feel more legitimate. It was originally styled as Mk.I - meaning "Mark 1", or version 1. I only intended to release just the 1 yoyo at first, but I had a lot of fun with the whole process so I kept working on new ideas.

What does a day in the life look like for you running Mk1 YoYo?

I don't "run" it daily. I have spurts of creative energy where I draft/design/finish a couple yoyo ideas, or I work on logos, packaging, or other bits that go into making a yoyo.

I have a checklist that I work through for preparing a new release, and once everything is ready I place all the orders for things I need. The busiest time is leading up to a release - coordinating retailer orders, social media posts, website setup, and email marketing - and usually a week or so after a release I can get back to the slow cadence of normality.

Walk me through your creative process.

Yoyo concepts can come from a couple places - either a shape I saw or imagined, or an idea one of my team members had, or a market niche that I want to find something for. I do most of my work digitally, first drafting in FreeCAD and then checking visuals in Blender to see if the design has both the numerical and aesthetic features I am looking for.

Recently I am also trying to spend more time linking together the concept/yoyo/colorway/name into something cohesive. This usually means custom packaging, which is a whole separate big design process.

What’s your favorite memory of running Mk1?

Meeting tons of cool people at the US National yoyo contest, and seeing part of my team (and sometimes future team members) in person.

What’s your favorite release to date?

The Ring-Bearer. I got to work on something that I didn't even realize was possible until I emailed Middle-Earth Enterprises. Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit have been special to me since I was little. The yoyos came out beautifully and I'm excited to work more with this license in the future.

What’s your next release and what makes it so exciting?

The Asterisk, a signature yoyo for EOS44. It's always really cool working on a signature or collaboration yoyo - a lot of my best work has been with a tight feedback loop with another person. The design for this yoyo is 90% EOS, though.

Feedback on the prototypes has been really positive, and the packaging that me and EOS designed together has a lot of really cool & fun details.

What’s in store for Mk1 in the future?

Probably more Lord of the Rings themed stuff.

Definitely more tug-responsive yoyos.

Plenty of exciting collabs!

If you could go back and do one thing differently what would that be?

Order more of the PK Sliver colorway the first time around.

What sets Mk1 apart from others?

One of my long-term goals is to elevate yoyo-design as a discipline. I've done some work with this in the form of tutorial series and freely-available design files, but there's much more work to do!

Any advice for aspiring companies/creators?

Plan out your costs & sales estimates in a spreadsheet. Use very conservative estimates so that you don't get surprised.

title: MonkeyfingeR Design
content:
From MonkeyfingeR:

"Here at MonkeyfingeR we are throwers first. We are passionate about creating skill toys because we love skill toys. We constantly strive to design and create products that we, and hopefully you, find fun. If you are an advanced player or someone who is just beginning your journey, we have a skill toy that will speak to you."

title: Moose
content:
Moose is an Australian toy company founded in 1989 in Melbourne. During the late-1990s yo-yo craze, Moose became the leading yo-yo brand in Australia, producing two series of novelty yo-yos marketed to children between approximately 1998 and 2001. The first series featured scented, chrome, glow-in-the-dark, and glitter plastic yo-yos numbered 1000–4000; the second series introduced a reflective finish line numbered 5000–7000. Each model was packaged with a trick instruction booklet.

The yo-yo line was discontinued in the early 2000s as the yo-yo boom subsided. The parent company, Moose Toys Pty Ltd, remains active as a toy manufacturer known for Mighty Beanz, Shopkins, and other collectible lines.

title: Motion YoYo
content:
From Motion:

"So, what’s the point of Motion YoYo?

I wanted to start a YoYo company that focuses not only on the playability of a YoYo, but also the aesthetics. I can say with all certainty that if a YoYo doesn’t jive with you by the way it looks and feels, it probably won’t find its way into your hands as often as it should.

I didn’t start Motion to be the “best” YoYo company in the world, but my hope is that the designs that crank out of our brand somehow find their way into your hand. My goal is helping you produce some of the best tricks you have ever thrown. Maybe you are more of a collector and this will find its way on your shelf as a display piece. Whatever the path, I want you to have a premium experience with every interaction that we share together.

At the end of the day, I just want you to open the box, wrap the string on your finger, and have a smile on your face every time you throw that breakaway.

- this is Motion "

title: Mr. Mazal Top’s Yoyos*
content:
Mr. Mazal Top's Yoyos is an independent, one-person yoyo brand based in South Texas, producing small-batch direct-to-consumer throws since 2020. The brand is known for affordable performance-grade 7068 aluminum bimetal designs and claims to be the first to offer bulk wooly nylon strings for the yoyo community.

* Editorial Note on Brand Status & Controversy While Mazal Top YoYos initially gained traction for its high-quality hybrid ceramic bearings, strings, and custom throws, the brand effectively ceased reliable operations by late 2023. Dozens of documented community reports from platforms like YoYoExpert and Reddit detail a pattern of unfulfilled orders, unissued refunds, and an eventual complete breakdown in communication. In 2025, it was brought to light within the community that the owner’s extended absence and business negligence were connected to an incarceration for domestic abuse. This section is maintained for historical context, but consumer discretion is heavily advised.

title: National Yo-Yo & Bo-Lo Co
content:
National Yo-Yo and Bo-Lo Co, Ltd. was a Canadian maker of wooden yo-yos. The YoYo Wiki gives its yo-yo years as 1960 to 1969, while the Yo-Yo Museum places sales of its Toronto-made Olympic and Pro Tournament models in 1968-77. The wiki lists three models: the Jeweled Satellite, Olympic and Pro Tournament. Its founding year is unknown.
It is a separate company from Cheerio Yo-Yo & Bo-Lo Company, the Kitchener, Ontario maker that Duncan acquired in 1954. The archive lists the Jewelled Satellite under Cheerio, while the YoYo Wiki credits it to National.

title: Novastage
content: Novastage is a Chinese yo-yo brand whose models reached Western and Japanese retailers in 2026. Retailers describe a line themed on the Investiture of the Gods, including the Nezha, a signature yo-yo of the Chinese champion Zhu Hang Feng, as well as the Daji and Yang Jian. It appears to be related to YoYo Empire, but that link is unproven. Its history is not independently documented.

title: OFFSET
content: OFFSET is an Australian competitive yo-yo brand founded in 2020 by Brandon Vu from his apartment during COVID lockdowns. What began as a one-person operation — Brandon handling video production, tuning, and order fulfillment himself — grew into one of the most prominent brands in modern competitive play. Built around Brandon's YouTube presence (Australia's largest yo-yo channel), OFFSET expanded to a pro team that includes Xavier Ng (multiple Singapore National Champion) and Allon Chen (multiple Australian National Champion). The brand is known for pushing width and performance boundaries, regularly releasing signature throws used to win national and world championships.
