meta.yya_company_profile:
OhYesYo (OYY) is a Baltimore, Maryland yo-yo brand created and owned by Coffin Nachtmahr, the subject of the documentary THROW. Coffin draws every design on graph paper first and favors mid-weight distribution.

The brand's first yo-yos, the Acrylic Echelons, were made by Landon Balk of 3Y03 and sold at VA States in January 2014. OYY is best known for the Echelon, Nightingale and Hearse, and for collaborations with One Drop (Eclipse, Lunar Eclipse), Rain City Skills (Sk8r), Ilinx Toys (Freq.Mod), 2Sick (Knight & Gale) and Fallen44 (The Witching Hour).

title: One Drop YoYos
content:
One Drop YoYos has been designing and building high end spinning toys in-house in Eugene, Oregon, USA since 2007.

They're a full-service shop, creating all their products in-house.

title: Only Pink Yoyos Company
content: Only Pink Yoyos (OPYOYOS) is a UK-based boutique yo-yo brand founded in 2019 by Jordan Blofeld of Brighton, England, as the spiritual successor to his previous company Smashing YoYos. The brand produces high-performance, limited-run monometal and bimetal yo-yos machined from 7068 aluminum — all exclusively in pink colorways. OPYOYOS releases are made in small numbered editions of around 30 units, distributed through contests and select retailers.

title: Pachyderm Yoyos
content: Pachyderm Yoyos specializes in custom 3D-printed yoyos and prototypes. Choose from our pre-made designs or send your unique idea for us to design and print.

title: Papa Jim’s Yo-yos & Tops
content: Papa Jim's Yo-yos & Tops was a handcrafted wooden toy business run by Jim Hilburger in Colden, western New York, documented in a 1999 woodturners' article. Its yo-yos were slightly oversized with a large axle, in butterfly and classic shapes, including a Papa Jim's Imperial. Founding year and current status are unknown.

title: Paragon Yoyos
content: About Paragon YoyosParagon Yoyos is a Southern California yo-yo brand founded by Eric Ngu, a longtime competitive player and member of the Crucial team. The company — registered as Hello Paragon LLC in El Monte, California in July 2024 — launched with a founding pair of precision-machined aluminum yo-yos: the Thou and the Zephyr. The two models were designed as deliberate contrasts, with the Thou embodying a smooth, organic, floaty character and the Zephyr offering a harder-lined, aggressive counterpart. Paragon subsequently collaborated with Crucial on the Sorbet, a polycarbonate-and-aluminum hybrid that extends the Milky's hybrid design language into a performance-first format. The brand ships worldwide.

title: Peter Fish
content: Peter Fish is an Australian company that a 2003 trademark record places in Mt Kuring-gai, New South Wales. The YoYo Wiki says it began in 1984, a date not independently confirmed, and describes its yo-yos as made in China by the same maker as Yomega. Documented models include the Dominator and Luminator, and the Smithsonian holds a Peter Fish Glow Pamela yo-yo. Its current status is unverified.

title: Playmaxx
content: Playmaxx, Inc. was a Tucson, Arizona yo-yo manufacturer founded in 1976 as Duncraft (soon renamed Duracraft, then Playmaxx in 1988) by Donald F. Duncan, Jr., son of Duncan Toys founder Donald F. Duncan Sr. Later run by Tom Van Dan Elzen and his son Hans "YoHans" Van Dan Elzen, Playmaxx's ProYo line became one of the best-selling fixed-axle and early transaxle yo-yo families of the 1990s yo-yo boom, expanding into the aluminum Cold Fusion and Ace series and the patented Brake Pad response system used across its Turbo Bumble Bee, ProFire, and Vid-e-Yo models. Products were co-branded and distributed internationally through partners including Hasbro (Koosh) and Bandai (Hyper Loop, Japan). Duncan Toys acquired Playmaxx's assets in late 2001; former Playmaxx principals Hans Van Dan Elzen and Ben McPhee went on to found YoYoFactory in 2003.

title: Pocket Pros
content:
Pocket Pros was a yo-yo product line introduced by Razor USA, LLC in 2010. Best known for its Razor scooters, Razor launched Pocket Pros alongside its consumer products as a mass-market yo-yo brand targeting youth retail channels. The lineup ran from a fixed-axle beginner model at $4.99 through an aluminum unresponsive yo-yo (the Zombie) at $19.99 — positioning itself as an accessible entry point into modern string-trick play.

The line included novelty models with real insects and arachnids encased in transparent acrylic (the Creeper and Stinger series), a centrifugal-clutch auto-return model (Boomerang), and intermediate plastic models with proprietary "18K Gold Pro" gold-plated bearings. Pocket Pros sponsored several yo-yo events including the 2010 California State Contest. The line was discontinued around 2011–2012; pocket-pros.com began redirecting to razor.com before the domain eventually lapsed.

title: Polyform
content: Polyform released the A4, a 6061 aluminum yo-yo with a nylon ring, in April 2023, and followed with the DEMA, the signature yo-yo of the sponsored player Jacky Le. Spintek describes the A4 as discontinued. Its founder announced the brand in March 2023. A link to Spintek is suggested by shared web addresses but is not stated by either brand.

title: Pop! Yoyos
content:
Based out of the Pacific Northwest but with a global player base, Pop! Yoyos aims to develop yoyos that embody the joy of the hobby while innovating with new, creative designs that help push the community forward. They focus on making fun, powerful, and stable throws that encourage creativity at all levels.

Alongside collaboration to further knit yoyoers together, Pop! stands by its motto: Passion Over Power, and exists to provide works of art that help players of all experience levels express themselves through the yoyoing lifestyle.

title: PoryKon
content: PoryKon is a professional 5A counterweight brand founded in Hong Kong in 2018 by six-time Hong Kong 3A national champion Ng Wang Kit ("Lowhand") and eight-time Hong Kong 5A national champion Denny Ko Kwan Ho. The name derives from Pokémon No. 137, Porygon — both share a polyhedral form and similar pronunciation in Cantonese.The brand originated in June 2018 when Denny Ko, while practicing for the Asia Pacific contest, found that standard counterweights would knot on the string and prove difficult to remove during complex tricks. He and Ng Wang Kit developed a bearing-integrated counterweight from scratch. A functional prototype was finalized on August 7, 2018, tested at WYYC 2018, and the original PoryKon bearing counterweight was released commercially in October 2018.PoryKon's signature innovation is the bearing system built into the counterweight body, which auto-adjusts string tension and dramatically reduces knot accumulation — a fundamental problem in 5A (counterweight) yo-yo play. Since then the brand has expanded into a full counterweight ecosystem spanning POM, polycarbonate, 3D-printed nylon, SLA resin, and dual-material (PC + silicone O-ring) designs. Signature models have been developed for Sora Ishikawa (5A World Champion), Hiroyasu Ishihara "PON," Naoki Uemae, Jacob Cheng Hongye, Denny Ko, Simpson Wong, and Korean champion Jihoo Lee. In 2020, PoryKon collaborated with C3yoyodesign to produce the Porycrash — their only yo-yo.

title: Project Cosmos
content: South Korean yo-yo manufacturer founded in 2024. Project Cosmos focuses on nostalgic monometal designs with modern daily-player performance. Founded by Korean players; distributes through 44emporium and Spinkult.

title: Quocrea
content: Quocrea is a Vietnam-based 5A yo-yo gear brand founded by Quoc Anh, a competitive 5A player who placed 9th in the 5A division at the 2026 World Yo-Yo Contest (Quoc Anh's own bio also states three Vietnam National Championship titles, unverified independently). The brand's Shopify store went live in mid-2026 with the Stand Apart Series, headlined by the Square Apart counterweight: a hybrid-construction 5A counterweight built around the QA (Quoc Axis) Lock System, a threaded interface that lets players swap between polycarbonate and POM halves on the same body to change weight and response.

title: R2FG
content: R2FG, said to stand for "Rotation To Fight Gravity", is a yo-yo maker in Shenzhen, China. YoYoExpert's launch post says it was founded in 2017. Its Euclase appeared in China in 2019, and in 2022 it launched the Riesenwellen sub-brand. Other models include the Ion Cannon, Deduction and Recluse.

title: Radical Seas
content: Radical Seas is an American yo-yo brand founded by Jamelle Kent and based in Texas. The brand built a reputation for clean, performance-focused designs built on the philosophy of simplicity and execution over complication — doing fewer things better. Their catalog spans mono-metal and bi-metal models, including collaborations with 2SickYoYos and Freshly Dirty. Active from 2015 through 2019.

title: Rain City Skills
content:
Rain City Skills was a skill toy company based in Vancouver, BC, founded in the fall of 2016 by Jeremy "Mr. Yoyothrower" McKay. Jeremy is a Canadian 4A champion (PNWR 4A and Canadian Nationals), and came to Rain City after years of involvement with King Yo Star. Inspired by a road trip to the One Drop shop in Eugene, Oregon, and encouraged by his wife to start a "hipster-themed yoyo company" bridging Vancouver and Oregon, Jeremy launched Rain City with their first throw, the Hipster Highlife.

The brand was known for machined-in-Oregon, designed-in-Vancouver yo-yos, begleri, and an extensive library of tutorial videos. Rain City Skills closed in April 2025.

If you have additional info on the Released/Retired dates, please email us at [email removed].

title: Recess
content: Maker of yoyos and apparel. We take fun seriously.

title: Return Bottoms
content: Return Bottoms is the brain-child of Andy (@audreysickburn on YYE) of Sickburn Yo-yo Workshop fame. This time, instead of 3D-printed yo-yos, they are selling machined yo-yos, special bearing blanks, and even No-Jive compatible axle sleeves.

title: Reykjavik Return Tops
content: Reykjavik Return Tops was an Icelandic yo-yo company whose owner, Palli, announced in May 2023 that it was closing, according to YoYoExpert. YoYoExpert lists its Mjolnir as the second release and first bimetal, named for Thor's hammer. The first release is not named in the sources found.

title: Riforgiate Design
content:
Riforgiate Design is a small yo-yo company founded by Gregg, a machinist based in California. Inspired by the yo-yos he played in the late 1990s and early 2000s, Gregg began designing and CNC-machining yo-yos himself. He announced his first prototype run on the YoYoExpert Forums in late 2024, seeking community support for his new brand. The designs take cues from classic late-90s/early-2000s shapes, updated for modern unresponsive play.

If you have additional info on the Released/Retired dates, please email us at [email removed].

title: RiHara
content: RiHara is a Chinese premium yo-yo design brand founded circa 2015 by designer Zhang Wenlin, operating under the tagline "Touch the Simplicity." The brand began under the name 7yoyodesign before rebranding to RiHara after the first arc units shipped — a deliberate repositioning as a premium design house. RiHara operated two lines: the RiHara Major Line for high-end and bimetal throws (ino), and RiHara Light for top-level performance at accessible price points (arc AIR series).The arc became a sought-after collector piece — particularly early green-logo silver-blasted units from the 7yoyodesign era — and RiHara's minimalist, curve-driven design philosophy influenced the broader premium Chinese yo-yo scene. A 2017 industry article cited the brand as a design reference, noting that SF Yoyos followed "a RiHara-esque design." RiHara also collaborated with TopYo on the Black Bird, designed by Zhang Wenlin, bringing the RiHara aesthetic to an accessible $32 price point.The brand ceased active operations sometime after 2016. The rihara.com domain is now listed for sale and all known products are in discontinued or museum status at Rewind, the brand's primary Western distributor.

title: Roll Out
content: Italian yo-yo manufacturer known for exclusive, limited-run high-end aluminum models. Small yet ferocious operation producing groundbreaking, original designs with extremely limited production runs.

title: Round Spinning Objects
content:
From RSO:

"Inspired by the coolest trick of it’s time.

The UFO trick was one of the first tricks we all learned back in the day before unresponsive return tops were a thing.  It wasn’t only visually stunning to see the return top flipped sideways spinning like a “flying saucer,” it was how you managed string tension. 

Although all return tops spin, there is only one Round Spinning Objects."

title: Royal Tops Manufacturing Company
content: Royal Tops Manufacturing Company was founded in 1937 in Long Island City, NY, by Joe "Chico" Radovan, a former Duncan yo-yo demonstrator. Its wooden yo-yos carried a crown-and-chevron logo and the Chico nickname (Chico Super Deluxe). In 1965, Royal Tops won a landmark trademark case against Donald F. Duncan, Inc., successfully arguing that "yo-yo" was a generic term in the Philippines and could not be exclusively owned — but the legal costs of the litigation forced both companies into bankruptcy that same year.

title: Russell
content: The Jack Russell Company was founded in 1947 by Jack Russell, a former Duncan Toys demonstrator who purchased the international promotions division he had built alongside Donald F. Duncan Sr. For over five decades, Russell became the world's dominant promotional yo-yo brand, producing advertising yo-yos for Coca-Cola and its sub-brands in 95 countries and igniting mass yo-yo crazes across the globe — most memorably in the 1980s. Renamed Russell Promotions, Inc. in 1997, the company continued producing limited runs for McDonald's, Volkswagen, Bandai, Daft Punk, and other brands. Jack Russell died in March 2004; the company remains nominally active under family management in Stuart, Florida.

title: Sengoku Yoyos
content:
Sengoku is a yoyo brand based in Aichi, Japan. The idea is to make high-performance yoyos. 

"Sengoku" is a period in Japanese history marked by near-constant military conflict. It ended when all political power was unified under the shogunate.

The yoyos will have the names of the most important rulers of the Samurai clans involved in that period.

title: SENSE YOYO
content: SENSE YOYO is a China-based yo-yo brand founded by Yiwen Li and Jiale Tong, originally launched in November 2019 as YoYoPalace (YYP) with the competition-oriented "Code" model. The brand rebranded to SENSE around 2021–2022, with the Mimic model marking the transition ("YYP's last farewell, SENSE's first greeting"). SENSE sponsors a roster of competitive throwers across Asia with signature models, including Jihoo Lee (South Korea, formerly — later moved to C3yoyodesign), Ahmad Kharisma (Indonesia), Quoc Anh (Vietnam), and twins Qin Ruiwen / Qin Ruian (China). The brand has no standalone official website and sells exclusively through third-party retailers including Yo-Yo Store Rewind, YoYoSam, and Spinkult.

title: SF Yoyos
content: "We make yoyos. No ridiculous descriptions of the yoyo superpowers they’ll give you… because they won’t. They spin. You know the drill and what you like… so check out the yoyo pages, watch the team do some tricks, peep the hashtag #sfyoyos and maybe pick one up if it looks like something you’d be into. We’d love to see you slaying some combos on them because that’s what we make em for."

title: Shenzhou
content: Shenzhou (神州, Shénzhōu — “Divine Land”) is a toy manufacturer based in the Chenghai district of Shantou, Guangdong, China — the historic center of Chinese toy manufacturing. Founded in 1988 as a plastics factory, the company entered the toy industry after China’s WTO accession in 2001, incorporating as Shantou Shenzhou Toys Co., Ltd. (汉头市神州玩具有限公司). By 2011 Shenzhou had released a line of hobbyist-grade metal and polycarbonate yo-yos — the Assault, Battle Axe, BlitzFire, Crystal, and Professional — sold internationally via Amazon and eBay, all featuring hubstacks and silicone O-ring response. The company subsequently shifted its primary focus to speed cubes while continuing to produce yo-yos as part of a broader toy portfolio, including aluminum alloy models and licensed consumer products.

title: Shinwoo
content: Shinwoo is a South Korean yo-yo manufacturer founded in 1987, known for offering ball-bearing yo-yos at aggressive price points. Its catalog spans budget plastic string-trick throws (Techno, Phantom, Loop series), off-string/multi-style models (ZanNavi, Griffin Wing, ProWing), and the Zen line of low-cost full-metal yo-yos. The Griffin Wing was used by Naoto Okada to win the 2009 4A World Championship.

title: Shuriken Yoyos
content: Shuriken Yoyos is a Hong Kong-designed brand whose models are named for Japanese throwing-star types. Its founder says it began in early 2021. The Juji and Senban followed, then the Happo in 2022 and the Roppo in 2023. Its current status is unknown.

title: Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop
content: Andy is a full time software development engineer and part time mad yoyo scientist. One of Andy’s favorite things is creating yoyos that look like they shouldn’t work at all yet somehow play well. A fan of fixed axle 0a and classic small bearing throws, Andy strives to live the life of a Frankensteinesque monster concocted from the best parts of Tom Kuhn, Audrey Hepburn, and various other pop culture fixations. When not 3d printing yoyos, spending time with their wife and two kids, or working, you can find Andy staring at household objects wondering if they can be turned into yoyos.

title: SKF
content: SKF is the Swedish bearing manufacturer, founded in 1907 and headquartered in Gothenburg. The Yo-Yo Museum documents ball-bearing "ROYO" yo-yos from the mid-1980s, dated roughly 1984-86, which the YoYo Wiki calls among the first ball-bearing yo-yos. Their promotional purpose is speculative. SKF is a bearing company that made yo-yos only incidentally.

title: Sleeper
content: Sleeper is the "pre-brand" of the yo-yo creator, Leo. Sleeper is currently working on funding his brand with the release of the Kaizoku.

title: Smashing Yo-Yo Company
content: Smashing YoYo Company was a UK brand run by Jordan Blofeld, which Yo-Yo Store REWIND dates to 2016 with operations ending in 2019. Its first release was the Poppet. The Kubrick was a prototype from its active period that was released in October 2023, after the company had stopped.

title: Sochi
content: Sōchí Company was founded in 2018 by Luckey Yulin Li, a five-time Canadian National Champion, and business partner Josef Chung. Building on a reputation for competition-grade strings, bearings, and response pads endorsed by multiple world champions including 2023 World Champion Mir Kim, Sochi expanded into original and collaborative yoyo designs. Their catalog spans dedicated 2A loopers, signature 1A competition throws, and unconventional hybrid designs in partnership with JIGUN, Unparalleled, and the Lab Exploration Program.

title: sOMEThING
content: sOMEThING by YoYoAddict is a Japanese premium yo-yo brand founded in 2012 by Hiroyuki "Mickey" Suzuki, the most decorated 1A competitor in World Yo-Yo Contest history — four world titles (2004, 2005, 2006, 2012), seven Asia-Pacific Championships, and six Japan National Championships. The brand operates as a sub-label of Suzuki's retail operation YoYoAddict, sold worldwide through Yo-Yo Store REWIND, YoYoExpert, and other major retailers.The mixed-case brand name encodes Suzuki's initials: lowercase "s" for Suzuki, lowercase "h" for Hiroyuki. The brand launched with the ANGLAM — its debut bi-metal combining a 6061 aluminum body with titanium weight rings — which immediately set a new standard for Japanese competition throws and seeded a product line that has run for over a decade. Every flagship ANGLAM variant has been used to win or place at the World Yo-Yo Contest.sOMEThING spans the premium and ultra-premium tiers of the market, from accessible aluminum monometals and plastic hybrids to full-titanium flagships above $900 USD. The brand's design philosophy centers on extreme rim weighting — using stainless steel, titanium, and POM rings positioned at the outer edge of the body — to maximize spin power and stability for high-speed, expressive competition freestyle. The lineup also includes dedicated 2A, 3A, and 4A models, and a signature series for team members Christopher Chia and Yuiga Suzuki.

title: Somewhere Designed Yoyos
content: Somewhere Designed Yoyos is a Japanese brand whose store lists the Somewhere, System Corp. and BB. Retailer descriptions link it to 44nollie, known for yo-yo tutorial and review videos, though its ownership, founding year and city are not established. Its models are monometals machined from 6061 aluminum.

title: Spectra Star
content: Spectra Star was a US company that, according to the YoYo Wiki, began in 1973 as a kite maker founded by Frank Alonso and started making yo-yos around 1982-83. Its yo-yos began with unlicensed sculpted-face "Radical Yos" lines, including the Globe "Earth Zone" and Leaping Lizard, and later included licensed designs such as Ghostbusters, Pee-wee Herman, Donald Duck and G.I. Joe. A contemporary kite trade advertisement supports its kite and yo-yo lines; the founding details and current status are unverified.

title: Spencer Berry YoYos
content: Spencer Berry is a legend in the yo-yo world. Former member of the Duncan Crew, Spencer discovered many of the tricks and elements that we all use today. Spencer, to date, has designed and released two yoyo’s, Walter & Theodore. According to Spencer’s website, there is a third yo-yo design in the works, Alice.

title: SpinGear
content:
About SpinGear
SpinGear (スピンギア) is a Tokyo-based yoyo specialty retailer and original equipment manufacturer founded and operated by Takahiko "Taka" Hasegawa, a Japanese National Yo-Yo Master and former world-class 4A (off-string) player. The company operates a physical store in Tokyo as well as an international e-commerce site at spingear.jp, selling products from manufacturers around the world.
Beyond retail, SpinGear designs and produces its own line of original yoyos under the SpinGear name, spanning beginner wooden and plastic models through intermediate and competition-level aluminum throws. The brand is best known for developing the SpinGadget — an affordable beginner polycarbonate yoyo that launched in December 2021 and spawned a large family of variants — and its Metal SpinGadget line aimed at intermediate players.
SpinGear also founded and operates the 66percent sub-brand (often written as 66%), which since 2017 has produced officially licensed miniaturized versions of iconic yoyos from other manufacturers (Duncan, YoYoFactory, YoYoFactory/Evan Nagao), machined to approximately 66% of their original scale entirely in Katsushika-ku, Tokyo. These micro-throws, typically around 37–38mm in diameter, are made in very limited quantities from stainless steel or aluminum and have developed a dedicated collector following.
SpinGear has collaborated with multiple brands including MagicYoYo (Katana M06, Katana 2), One Drop YoYos (American Metal SpinGadget), and video game publisher Arc System Works (Guilty Gear -STRIVE- Bridget Yo-Yo).

title: Spinkult
content: Spinkult is a yo-yo concept store and creative agency currently operating out of Malmö, Sweden, shipping worldwide. Rather than manufacturing its own line, Spinkult curates a selection from established brands (YoYoFactory, Oxygène, SF Yoyos, yoyorecreation, Smashing YoYo Company, and others) and periodically releases limited-run collaborative "Spinkult Edition" throws with those brands. The store also runs community events under the "Spinkult Seasons" banner. Note: a 2021 Museum of Yo-Yo History listing described spinkult.com as based in Russia; the current official site and socials place the store in Sweden, so an earlier relocation or rebrand is possible but unconfirmed.

title: Spintastics
content: Spintastics Skill Toys, Inc. grew out of Dale Oliver's "Science of Spin" school demonstration program. The Technic yo-yo he designed (first sold summer 1995) became the basis of the company; in 1996 Oliver partnered with fellow demonstrator Valerie Krantz to formally found Spintastics, incorporating in Euless, Texas by 1997. It became a top-5 U.S. yo-yo manufacturer, the only one at the time owned and designed by a world yo-yo champion, before expanding into spin tops and the U.S.-designed Spinabolo diabolo.The original owners sold the brand in pieces between 2015 and 2021 (to YoYoPlay, then to YoYoSam's Mitch Silver / MSE Enterprises), under whom it still operates today.Note: the company's current-day website states a 1993 founding date, which conflicts with its own period-correct (c.2000) history page and the Yo-Yo Museum's company profile, both of which place formal founding in 1995–1996. Unresolved discrepancy — flagged, not corrected.

title: Spintek
content: Spintek sells low-priced beginner yo-yos, with the stated aim of lowering the barrier to learning the basics. Retailers list it as designed in Canada, and its site says products are made through partner factories and tested to toy-safety standards. Its Revlo is described as based on the discontinued Polyform A4. Models include the Bowtie, Revlo and R1 Pro.

title: Spinworthy Yoyos
content:
Spinworthy is a manufacturer based in Adelaide, South Australia producing high quality handmade wooden yoyos.

The recently emerged modern fixed axle movement offers a fresh and challenging new style of yoyoing that honours its roots in the yoyos of yesteryear.

Spinworthy yoyos offer no compromises in quality and performance and are designed and hand made for the latest fixed axle tricks.

title: Spiral
content:
Throw Spiral is a boutique yo-yo brand founded in 2020 by Jamie, a designer with over a decade of experience testing prototypes for indie yo-yo brands. Jamie launched the brand with their first official release, the Kappa — a competitive organic yo-yo made from 7068 aluminum, designed to challenge the assumption that organic-shaped throws can't perform at a high level. Throw Spiral is recognizable for its signature Spiral rim groove aesthetic detail and manga-inspired branding (Instagram: @throwspiral, styled as "Spiral's Bizarre Adventure").

Notable releases include the Kappa (2020, with player colorways for Matt Doyle and Adrian Esteban) and the Sliver, a slimline collaboration with MK1 Yoyos.

If you have additional info on the Released/Retired dates, please email us at [email removed].

title: SPUTNIK
content: SPUTNИK is an independent boutique yo-yo brand founded July 2, 2024. The name means "fellow traveler, companion, or satellite" — evoking both the astronomical object and the idea of a yo-yo orbiting the hand. The brand distributes through YoYoExpert and YoYoSam.

title: SPYY
content: SPYY (Saturn Precision Yo-Yos) was a boutique Canadian yo-yo manufacturer based in Calgary, Alberta. Founded by mechanical engineer Steve Buffel — who began experimenting with yo-yo design as a side project at his motorsports engineering firm in 2003 — the company launched its first consumer products in early 2006 and quickly earned a reputation for precision machining, tight tolerances, and thoughtful design. All SPYY yo-yos were manufactured in Canada.The brand built a world-class team including Guy Wright, Ed Haponik, Alexis JV, Nate Sutter, Sebastian Brock, and Jonathan Robinson. SPYY collaborated with fellow Canadian company CLYW on the Galactic Goose, and with wood yo-yo maker TMBR on the annual eH fixed-axle signature series for Ed Haponik. The company officially closed on July 20, 2013, having shipped approximately 10,000 yo-yos over its lifetime. Buffel returned in 2015 with the limited TYY-01 titanium release and continued the eH wood series through 2016.

title: Square Wheels
content: Kansas City based YoYo Company with high quality and artistic expression paramount in the design process.

title: Static Co.
content: Thoughtfully curated yoyo releases and other items. Based in UT, USA.

title: Sturm Panzer
content: Sturm Panzer is a Japanese yo-yo brand, launched as a project in autumn 2012 with commercial brand operations beginning January 1, 2013. Each yoyo release is paired with an illustrated storybook/manga ("Yo-Yo Fist," an alt-history combat-sport series), with concept and original story credited to G&K and principal illustration (from volume 6/new volume 1 through the final volume 14, concluding December 2018) by Tsugumi Suzuma. The brand has continued releasing yoyos after the main storyline's conclusion, with new models confirmed as recently as June 2026.Sturm Panzer SS ("Side-Story"), a sub-brand launched October 14, 2020, is notable for the SS-001 Mini Panzer, marketed as the world's smallest metal production yoyo. The SS line is produced by former Team YoYoJam member ZhaoYuan Liu ("PHENOM").Founding date and exact HQ location beyond "Japan-based" are not independently confirmable beyond what's stated here.

title: SuperYo
content: SuperYo was founded in 1994 by Arne Dixon, a former Duncan yo-yo demonstrator who had spent years performing and teaching at schools across the United States. Based in Lynnwood, Washington, the company was notable for owning its entire manufacturing process end-to-end, including all machinery — a rarity among small toy manufacturers of the era. SuperYo initially produced all its yo-yos domestically in the USA, later outsourcing portions of production to Chinese factories as the boom years wound down.The company’s product philosophy was engineering-forward. Several SuperYo models introduced genuinely novel mechanisms: the patented IntelliGap axle system allowed string gap adjustment by twisting the halves without losing small parts; the Typhoon introduced the first plastic ball bearing in a production yo-yo; and the Samurai featured one of the first ceramic bearings in any production yo-yo, along with diamond-finish CNC-machined aluminum halves toleranced to ±0.0005″.SuperYo was deeply embedded in the late 1990s yo-yo performance and competition circuit. In 1999, Arne Dixon produced “Kickin’ Tricks,” a landmark instructional video featuring Doctor Popular, Jennifer Baybrook, David Capurro, and Steve Brown, shot on location at the 1999 American Nationals and the 1999 World Yo-Yo Contest. The Samurai held a documented sleep record of twelve minutes and two seconds at time of release.From the early 2000s onward, SuperYo became closely tied to The NED Show — Dixon’s educational character-building assembly program for K–6 schools. The NED acronym (Never give up, Encourage others, Do your best) became the company’s primary identity. The yo-yo brand faded as NED Show yo-yos became the main product output, with production appearing to wind down entirely by the mid-2010s.

title: SUS YOYO MECHANICS
content: SUS YOYO MECHANICS is a Japanese yo-yo design brand built around the philosophy of creating things that exceed expectations — expressed in Japanese as "望まれたものを望まれた以上の物にする." The brand operates as a design studio whose creator's identity has been intentionally kept undisclosed. SUS produces its own original lineup under the SUS0XX numbering system and has collaborated extensively with YoYoFactory (as the Japan Design Studio), Yo-Yo Store REWIND, Caribou Lodge, and Top Yo.

title: Takara Tomy
content: Takara Tomy is a Japanese toy company formed by the 2006 merger of Takara and Tomy. Its yo-yo releases were occasional. The YoYo Wiki lists Pocketmate yo-yos from 1975, and the Yo-Yo Museum shows the Screw Ball, a Japanese version of Abbe Toys' Black Mamba, as a Tomy product from 1997, before the merger. In 2022 it released the Mugen Yo-Yo, a battery-powered yo-yo that connects to a smartphone app.

title: Takuto.Design
content: Takuto.Design was a Chinese maker of limited-run aluminum yo-yos owned by Yicheng Luo, according to the YoYo Wiki, which lists it as defunct. Its first production model, the Hurricane, appeared in 2006 and was affordable enough to sell widely in mainland China. A retailer notes the L4 in 2009 and the L5 several years later, so the company's end date is uncertain.

title: Team Losi
content: Team Losi was primarily a radio-control vehicle maker. In 1998 it hired Steve Brown to design yo-yos during the boom, according to Brown's own account on the Yo-Yo Museum site. Its first yo-yos were sold as Revolution Yo-Yos, followed by Team Losi's own Da Bomb, Cherry Bomb and Grim Sleeper, and it also supplied two designs to Variflex. Brown left for Duncan in 1999, and the yo-yo line ended after the company was sold. Brown recalls a 2001 sale, while Horizon Hobby dates its merger to 2000.

title: The Good Life
content: By players for players

title: Thesis Yoyos
content: Thesis Yoyos was founded in 2017 by Shivum Berry in Irvine, California. Built around elevated presentation — premium packaging, minimalist aesthetics, and accessories — the brand set out to deliver boutique yoyo quality without boutique pricing. Thesis built its identity around detail-oriented design philosophy rather than spec saturation, and became widely recognized through the Serenade, a Colin Nguyen signature Delrin that rivaled bimetals at its price point, and the SynThesis / HypoThesis / AnTiThesis naming arc that ran from the brand's debut mono-metal through its titanium flagship.

title: Throw Down
content: Throw Down was created and owned by Nate Weddle. Nate also was responsible for the aluminum Duncan Freehand weight rings. As of 2009 Throw Down has been closed.

title: Throw Revolution
content: Throw Revolution is a Singapore-based premium yo-yo brand founded by World Champion Marcus Koh. Specializing in high-performance aluminum and bi-metal yo-yos, the brand is known for innovative designs and competitive-grade precision. All products are designed with 1A string trick performance in mind.

title: Throw Spiral
content: Throw Spiral was introduced by its founder, Jamie Larkins, in May 2020, according to a YoYoExpert forum thread. Its Kappa is described as a competitive organic-profile yo-yo with a V-shaped inner profile. Retailers also list signature editions and a collaboration with MK1 Yoyos. Its current status is unverified.

title: Throw-Yo Threads
content:
Throw-Yo is a boutique yo-yo string brand run by Berv Throwington. Every string is handmade: blended, wound, and cut by hand. The product scope is narrow on purpose. Strings, counterweights, and stickers. That's it.

The catalog is organized into four families: Comfort, Performance, Responsive, and Specials. Each one named from a taxonomy of chemistry, nature, and process. Vapor. Detergent. Pollen. Ink. Names that earn their place or don't make it in.

Counterweights are poured from recycled plastisol in five shapes: Skull, Fruiting Body, Grey Matter, Corvid, and Plaquette.

Once a year, Berv's wife walks into the thread room and picks. No brief. No spec. Whatever she wants. Berv winds it. Whatever comes out gets her name. It's called the Baroness Blend.

Emulsion Blends
